author.name: Michael Finkelson, Daniel Segal, Eitan Richardson, Shahar Armon, Nani Goldring, Poriya Panet, Nir Zabari, Benjamin Brazowski, Or Patashnik, Yoav HaCohen

entry.summary: ScenA conditions a text-to-audio flow-matching foundation model on multiple reference voices and a free-form scene prompt to generate realistic multi-speaker audio scenes including background noise, room acoustics, and overlapping dialogue. It moves beyond clean speech-only pipelines toward in-the-wild conversational audio.

entry.title: VEGA: Learning Navigation VLAs from In-the-Wild Egocentric Video with Geometric Trajectory Supervision

author.name: Gershom Seneviratne, Yohan Abeysinghe, Jianyu An, Vaibhav Shende, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: VEGA trains navigation Vision-Language-Action models from unlabeled in-the-wild egocentric videos by reconstructing local scene geometry and generating obstacle-aware, goal-conditioned trajectories as supervision. It converts passive human walking videos into usable robot navigation data.

entry.title: Admittance-Based Surface Alignment for Human-in-the-Loop Robotic Visual Inspection

author.name: Antara Banerjee, Colin Acton, Xu Chen

entry.summary: DREAM-Chunk is a test-time scaling method that augments action-chunking VLA policies with a lightweight latent world model, sampling candidate chunks and selecting actions whose predicted latent futures best match observed rollouts. It improves robustness of open-loop chunk execution without policy fine-tuning.

entry.title: Scaling Hypothesis #2: Are Humans Just More Over-Parameterized?

author.name: gwern

entry.summary: Gwern's 2024 essay hypothesizes that human brains and LLMs differ via a bias-variance tradeoff: LLMs minimize variance while overparameterized human brains minimize bias through high-learning-rate training on small, highly-filtered data, catapulting to generalizing basins. If true, this suggests a scaling paradigm yielding far better generalization and adversarial robustness.

entry.title: MolmoMotion: Language-guided 3D motion forecasting

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Ai2 introduces MolmoMotion, an open language-guided 3D motion forecasting model that predicts how object points will move in the future. It is positioned to strengthen motion prediction for robotics, video generation, and other systems requiring forward reasoning about object dynamics.

entry.title: A Risk Decomposition Framework for Pre-Hoc Fine-Tuning Prediction

author.name: Yuxiang Luo, Chen Wang, Nan Tang

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical risk decomposition framework for pre-hoc fine-tuning performance prediction, separating prediction risk into an intrinsic limit and reducible optimization variance. It proves a necessary lower bound on optimization variance decay and derives a budget-optimal probing principle.

entry.title: Gaussian Mixture Attention: Linear-Time Sequence Mixing via Probabilistic Latent Routing

author.name: Yongchao Huang, Hassan Raza

entry.summary: Introduces Gaussian Mixture Attention (GMA), a linear-time attention-style mixer that routes queries and keys through K learned Gaussian mixture components via responsibility vectors, avoiding the N×N affinity matrix. Targets the long-context scaling bottleneck of standard attention.

entry.title: Quantifying Consistency in LLM Logical Reasoning via Structural Uncertainty

author.name: Baishali Chaudhury, Mengdie Flora Wang, Hyunji Hayley Park, Rahul Ghosh, Sungmin Hong, Jae Oh Woo

entry.summary: Proposes structural uncertainty, a consistency-aware framework that measures the stability of self-preference rankings over sampled reasoning paths rather than just output dispersion. It captures whether models can consistently rank competing reasoning candidates.

entry.title: Dissecting model behavior through agent trajectories

author.name: Gaurav Gupta, Vatshank Chaturvedi, Jun Huan, Anoop Deoras

entry.summary: Formalizes the intent-execution gap between what an agent model intends and what its harness executes, and develops a customizable Simple Strands Agent to study harness-model alignment. It argues harness design is as critical as the model itself.

entry.title: Beyond Domains: Reusing Web Skills via Transferable Interaction Patterns

author.name: Shiqi He, Yue Cui, Feijie Wu, Xinyu Ma, Jiaheng Lu, Yaliang Li, Bolin Ding, Mosharaf Chowdhury

entry.summary: Proposes reusing web agent skills via transferable interaction patterns rather than instruction similarity, improving skill reuse on held-out sites to reduce steps and tokens. It targets latency and cost in web agents on benchmarks like Mind2Web and WebArena.

entry.title: TrustErase: Auditable Instant Machine Unlearning with Passport-Embedded Representations

author.name: Rutger Hendrix, Leonardo G. Russo, Concetto Spampinato, Matteo Pennisi, Giovanni Bellitto

entry.summary: TrustErase is a verifiable, data-free machine unlearning framework using passport-embedded representations as cryptographic keys within parameter-efficient adaptation layers. It enables instant, auditable forgetting of classes or datasets through deactivation without retraining.

entry.title: Visuals Lie, Consistency Speaks: Disentangling Spatial Attention from Reliability in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Logan Mann, Yi Xia, Ajit Saravanan, Ishan Dave, Saadullah Ismail, Shikhar Shiromani, Emily Huang, Ruizhe Li, Kevin Zhu

entry.summary: Challenges the assumption that tight visual attention signals VLM reliability through a cross-family study using structural-attention metrics like cluster counts and spatial entropy. It finds attention structure does not reliably predict trustworthiness, proposing consistency-based signals instead.

entry.title: AUTOGATE: Automated Clock Gating via Toggling-Aware LLM-based RTL Rewriting

author.name: Yiting Wang, Chenhui Deng, Chia-Tung Ho, Yanqing Zhang, Zhuo Feng, Cunxi Yu, Ang Li, Gang Qu, Brucek Khailany

entry.summary: AUTOGATE is an agentic framework for industry-grade RTL power optimization via toggling-aware LLM-based clock gating, using an ML-LLM co-design to bridge waveform analysis and RTL rewriting. It handles long waveform traces and large hierarchical codebases while preserving correctness.

entry.title: MagicSim: A Unified Infrastructure for Executable Embodied Interaction

author.name: Haoran Lu, Songling Liu, Yue Chen, Guo Ye, Mutian Shen, Shuyang Yu, Yu Xiao, Jihai Zhao, Shang Wu, Jianshu Zhang, Xiangtian Gui, Chuye Hong, Yuran Wang, Maojiang Su, Jiayi Wang, Ruihai Wu, Zhaoran Wang, Han Liu

entry.summary: MagicSim is a unified embodied interaction infrastructure built around a deterministic batched runtime and shared MDP, using YAML specifications to construct diverse executable worlds. It enables reproducible, evaluable, and annotatable episodes linking control, skills, and planning.

entry.title: See First, Answer Later: Visual Evidence Pre-Alignment via Sufficiency-Driven RL

author.name: Yilian Liu, Sicong Leng, Guoshun Nan, Junyi Zhu, Jiayu Huang, Minghao Sun, Xuancheng Zhu, Yisong Chen, Zexian Wei, Xiaofeng Tao

entry.summary: VEPA introduces Visual Evidence Pre-Alignment, an intermediate training stage using sufficiency-driven reinforcement learning to strengthen visual grounding in MLLMs before post-training. It addresses weak grounding from coarse caption pretraining that biases models toward salient objects.

entry.title: A Framework for Evaluating Agentic Skills at Scale

author.name: Maksim Shaposhnikov, Nicolas Fortuin, Simon Stipcich, Maria I. Gorinova, Amy Heineike, Rob Willoughby

entry.summary: Proposes a scalable evaluation framework for agent skills (reusable knowledge artifacts that augment LLM agents), letting authors build realistic tasks to assess skill utility, applied at scale to 500 real-world skills generating 1,000 tasks. Fills a gap in measuring individual skill value.

entry.title: Functional Equivalence in Attention: A Comprehensive Study with Applications to Linear Mode Connectivity

author.name: Viet-Hoang Tran, Vinh Khanh Bui, Van-Hoan Trinh, Tan Lai Ngoc, Tan M. Nguyen

entry.summary: Provides a formal study of functional equivalence (parameter symmetries) in Transformers with sinusoidal and rotary positional encodings, showing how these encodings reshape architectural symmetries with applications to linear mode connectivity. Extends symmetry theory to attention models.

entry.title: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Strategy Synthesis for Strategic Logics

author.name: Marco Aruta, Vadim Malvone, Aniello Murano, Domenico Parente, Luca Rizzuti

entry.summary: Introduces a neuro-symbolic framework where an LLM proposes candidate strategies for multi-agent strategic logics (e.g., ATL) that are then formally verified by a model checker. The generate-and-certify design preserves formal soundness while navigating large strategy spaces.

entry.title: Volterra Generative Models

author.name: Yusen Jia, Bingyan Han

entry.summary: Introduces Volterra generative models, a continuous-time score-based diffusion framework that injects path-dependent noise via fractional kernels, replacing memoryless Brownian perturbations. Constructs finite-dimensional Markovian lifts and proves error bounds for the non-Markovian dynamics.

entry.title: Learning Fair Pareto-Optimal Policies in Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Umer Siddique, Peilang Li, Yongcan Cao

entry.summary: Formalizes fair multi-policy multi-objective RL, learning a set of Pareto-optimal policies that ensure fairness via the generalized Gini welfare function across all possible user preferences. Provides theoretical contributions for fairness over preference space.

entry.title: Structural Role Injection in Handlebars-Templated LLM Prompts: Triple-Brace Interpolation, Delimiter Family, and the Limits of HTML Auto-Escaping

author.name: Mohammadreza Rashidi

entry.summary: Analyzes how Handlebars templating (the default in Microsoft Semantic Kernel) silently governs exposure to structural role injection attacks, since HTML escaping neutralizes angle brackets but not square brackets, colons, or Markdown used by ChatML and Llama-3 delimiters. Exposes a prompt-injection security vector in LLM applications.

entry.title: All Smoke, No Alarm: Oracle Signals in Agent-Authored Test Code

author.name: Dipayan Banik, Kowshik Chowdhury, Shazibul Islam Shamim

entry.summary: Empirically studies 86,156 agent-authored test-file patches to determine whether AI-generated tests contain meaningful verification logic (oracle signals) and how this links to merge outcomes and review effort. Shows test-file presence overestimates verification strength.

entry.title: Attribution-Guided and Coverage-Maximized Pruning for Structural MoE Compression

author.name: Yifu Ding, Jiacheng Wang, Ge Yang, Yongcheng Jing, Jinyang Guo, Xianglong Liu, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Proposes attribution-guided, coverage-maximized structural pruning for Mixture-of-Experts models, observing that information concentrates in a small subset of channels within experts so channel-level pruning captures redundancy missed by expert-level methods. Achieves finer-grained MoE compression.

entry.title: LLMZero: Discovering Adaptive Training Strategies for RL Post-Training via LLM Agents

author.name: Haoyang Fang, Wei Zhu, Boran Han, Alex Zhang, Zhenyu Pan, Shuo Yang, Shuai Zhang, Jiading Gai, Peng Tang, Cuixiong Hu, Xuan Zhu, Huzefa Rangwala, George Karypis, Bernie Wang

entry.summary: LLMZero uses LLM agents to search over RL post-training trajectories via tree search, diagnosing pathologies and proposing coordinated parameter transitions. It uncovers an empirical pattern where capacity parameters grow monotonically while regularization parameters oscillate.

entry.title: What Does the Weight Norm Control in Grokking? Logit-Scale Mediation under Cross-Entropy

author.name: Truong Xuan Khanh

entry.summary: Investigates what the weight norm actually controls in grokking, showing via clamping experiments that the grokking delay collapses almost entirely onto the effective logit scale under cross-entropy. It finds the norm adds little beyond logit scale and the effect is loss-dependent.

entry.title: BLADE: Scalable Bi-level Adaptive Data Selection for LLM Training

author.name: Jiaxing Wang, Deping Xiang, Jin Xu, Zirui Liu, Zicheng Zhang, Guoqiang Gong, Jun Fang, Chao Liu, Pengzhang Liu, Tongxuan Liu, Ke Zhang, Qixia Jiang

entry.summary: BLADE is a Hessian-free bi-level adaptive data selection framework for LLM training that reformulates influence-based selection to avoid intractable inverse-Hessian computations while adapting to the evolving model. It aims to filter uninformative data and build adaptive learning trajectories at trillion-token scale.

entry.title: GateMem: Benchmarking Memory Governance in Multi-Principal Shared-Memory Agents

author.name: Zhe Ren, Yibo Yang, Yimeng Chen, Zijun Zhao, Benshuo Fu, Zhihao Shu, Bingjie Zhang, Yangyang Xu, Dandan Guo, Shuicheng Yan

entry.summary: GateMem is a benchmark for multi-principal shared-memory LLM agents that jointly evaluates utility, access control across authorization boundaries, and active forgetting after deletion requests across medical, office, education, and household domains. It addresses governance of shared memory pools beyond single-user assumptions.

entry.title: Semantic Robustness Certification for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Peiyu Yang, Paul Montague, Feng Liu, Andrew C. Cullen, Amardeep Kaur, Christopher Leckie, Sarah M. Erfani

entry.summary: Proposes a framework to certify vision-language model robustness under semantic-level transformations like shape, size, and style, using text prompts as semantic proxies parameterized by a controllable variation extent. It extends robustness certification beyond geometric and pixel-level changes.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Active Feature Acquisition via LLM-Elicitation

author.name: Binyamin Perets, Natalie Mendelson, Shiran Vainberg, Yehuda Chowers, Shai Shen-Orr, Shie Mannor

entry.summary: Develops a zero-shot active feature acquisition framework that elicits from an LLM only its trustworthy unary and pairwise statistics to construct a Markov random field guiding which features to observe, separating knowing from deciding. It applies to binary classification and top-k identification without labeled data.

entry.title: Be Your Own Teacher: Steering Protein Language Models via Unsupervised Reward Optimization

author.name: Lanqing Li, Shentong Mo, Yang Yu, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: Introduces unsupervised reward optimization for steering protein language models without ground-truth labels, using task-agnostic rewards combining intrinsic model uncertainty and extrinsic semantic consistency from protein representation models. It proposes offline algorithms for controllable protein generation that bypass costly wet-lab validation.

entry.title: Spotlight: Synergizing Seed Exploration and Spot GPUs for DiT RL Post-Training

author.name: Ruiqi Lai, Dakai An, Wei Gao, Ju Huang, Siran Yang, Jiamang Wang, Lin Qu, Dmitrii Ustiugov, Wei Wang

entry.summary: Spotlight is a systems framework that harvests cheaper spot GPUs for reinforcement learning post-training of Diffusion Transformers, combining seed exploration with spot GPU pipelining to overcome idle-time and preemption challenges. It substantially reduces the prohibitive cost of DiT RL post-training.

entry.title: TxBench-PP: Analyzing AI Agent Performance on Small-Molecule Preclinical Pharmacology

author.name: Hannah Le, Ramesh Ramasamy, Alex Urrutia, Mahsa Yazdani, Tim Proctor, Kenny Workman

entry.summary: TxBench-PP is a verifiable benchmark for evaluating AI agents on small-molecule preclinical pharmacology, testing whether agents recover accurate conclusions from real assay data rather than memorized literature facts. It is the first slice of a broader drug-discovery agent evaluation effort.

entry.title: JetFlow: Breaking the Scaling Ceiling of Speculative Decoding with Parallel Tree Drafting

author.name: Lanxiang Hu, Zhaoxiang Feng, Yulun Wu, Haoran Yuan, Yujie Zhao, Yu-Yang Qian, Bojun Wang, Daxin Jiang, Yibo Zhu, Tajana Rosing, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: JetFlow breaks speculative decoding's scaling ceiling with parallel tree drafting, resolving the causality-efficiency dilemma between autoregressive and bidirectional block-diffusion drafters. It improves acceptance length while keeping drafting cost low to accelerate LLM inference.

entry.title: Steerable Cultural Preference Optimization of Reward Models

author.name: Minsik Oh, Advit Deepak, Sophie Wu, Douwe Kiela, Ekaterina Shutova

entry.summary: This paper introduces SCPO, a reward model training algorithm that incorporates diverse cultural preferences in a balanced manner, aiming to represent subcommunity preferences without excessive bias toward any group. It advances LLM alignment with a more global, steerable cultural outlook.

entry.title: Beyond Reward Engineering: A Data Recipe for Long-Context Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xiaoyue Xu, Sikui Zhang, Xiaorong Wang, Xu Han, Chaojun Xiao

entry.summary: This paper takes a data-centric approach to long-context reinforcement learning, showing that a simple data recipe targeting retrieval, multi-evidence synthesis, and reasoning, paired with minimal outcome-based GRPO, substantially improves long-context reasoning. It contrasts with prior work focused on reward engineering.

entry.title: Reasoning as Intersection: Consensus-Frame Alignment for Visual Focus in Video-MLLMs

author.name: Chengwen Liu, Zhe Huang, Jisheng Dang, Hong Peng, Qi Tian, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Introduces CF-GRPO, a temporal-annotation-free process-level reward framework for video-MLLM reasoning that builds a consensus frame prior from intrinsic video cues and aligns model frame-use to visual evidence. Improves evidence-aware video reasoning over outcome-only rewards.

entry.title: Taming I2V models for Image HOI Editing: A Cognitive Benchmark and Agentic Self-Correcting Framework

author.name: Jiayi Gao, Qingchao Chen, Yuxin Peng, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces HOI-Edit, a benchmark with progressive cognitive levels and an automated VLM-based metric for evaluating image editing of human-object interactions, plus an agentic self-correcting framework using image-to-video models. It separates dynamic interaction validity from static attribute preservation.

entry.title: Splaxel: Efficient Distributed Training of 3D Gaussian Splatting for Large-scale Scene Reconstruction via Pixel-level Communication

author.name: Wenqi Jia, Zhewen Hu, Ying Huang, Yu Gong, Stavros Kalafatis, Yuke Wang, Wei Niu, Chengming Zhang, Ang Li, Sheng Di, Yuede Ji, Bo Fang, Miao Yin

entry.summary: Splaxel is a communication-efficient distributed 3D Gaussian Splatting training framework that renders local Gaussian subsets per GPU and exchanges only partial pixel values rather than synchronizing Gaussians. It maintains global consistency while reducing inter-GPU communication for large-scale scenes.

entry.title: HALOMI: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation with Active Perception from Human Demonstrations

author.name: Zehui Zhao, Yuxuan Zhao, Gaojing Zhang, Chenxi Liu, Maolin Zheng, Wenzhao Lian

entry.summary: HALOMI extends the Universal Manipulation Interface with egocentric sensing to learn humanoid loco-manipulation with active hand-eye perception from human demonstrations. It addresses brittle world-frame tracking and the human-to-humanoid gap in observation and action.

entry.title: A High-accuracy Event-based Underwater SLAM System

author.name: Yifan Peng, Qihang, Liu, Haoying Li, Yuzhe Li, Junfeng Wu, Ziyang Hong

entry.summary: Develops the first high-accuracy event-based underwater stereo SLAM system, using a structure-aware Time Surface metric and Bayesian-optimized two-stage TS generation to overcome velocity-dependent degradation and matching failures. It targets the harsh underwater environment where standard event TS methods fail.

entry.title: Object-Centric Residual RL for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real VLA Enhancement

author.name: Kinam Kim, Namiko Saito, Heecheol Kim, Katsushi Ikeuchi, Jaegul Choo, Yasuyuki Matsushita

entry.summary: Proposes an object-centric residual RL framework trained purely in simulation that refines frozen VLA actions using object poses to improve real-world robustness zero-shot. It sidesteps the sim-to-real dilemmas of privileged-state distillation, image-domain gaps, and costly real-world RL.

entry.title: TactSpace: Learning a Physics-enriched Shared Latent Space for Tactile Sim-to-Real Transfer

author.name: Arunim Joarder, Arjun Bhardwaj, Ren\'e Zurbr\"ugg, Mayank Mittal, Florin P\"untener, Sira Bielefeldt, Cosmin Roman, Vaishakh Patil, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: TactSpace learns a physics-enriched shared latent space aligning heterogeneous tactile modalities (e.g., simulated penetration depth and real capacitance) to enable tactile sim-to-real transfer without accurate raw-signal simulation. It uses modality-specific encoders projecting into a common space.

entry.title: Invertible Neural Network Adapter for One-Step Flow Matching in Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yu Zhang, Kangyi Ji, Yongxiang Zou, Rongtao Xu, Feng Zheng, Long Cheng

entry.summary: HT-Bench is a large-scale multi-task benchmark for dexterous full-hand tactile sensing paired with egocentric vision, comprising 10M RGB and 7.8M tactile frames across 226 tasks. It evaluates whether tactile representations encode contact geometry and align with visual information.

entry.title: The Implicit Bias of Steepest Descent with Mini-batch Stochastic Gradient

author.name: Jichu Li, Xuan Tang, Difan Zou

entry.summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the implicit bias of mini-batch stochastic steepest descent (which generalizes methods like SignSGD and Muon) in multi-class classification under various norm geometries. It shows that without momentum only full-batch gradients guarantee max-margin convergence, while momentum enables small-batch convergence via a batch-momentum trade-off.

entry.title: Treatment Response Optimized Clinical Decision Support AI System via Digital Twin Simulation

author.name: Xinyu Qin, Anil K. Sood, Ruiheng Yu, Sara Corvigno, Elaine Stur, Lu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes an online adaptive clinical decision support framework combining treatment effect estimation, patient digital twins, and reinforcement learning with rule-based safety monitoring. It targets real-time treatment adaptation under safety constraints.

entry.title: SEAGym: An Evaluation Environment for Self-Evolving LLM Agents

author.name: Congjie Zheng, Chuanyi Xue, Bin Liang, Jun Yang, Changshui Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces SEAGym, an evaluation environment for self-evolving LLM agents that measures harness updates across training, validation, replay, and cost dimensions. It exposes whether updates produce reusable improvement, overfit, or harm prior behavior.

entry.title: Translating the Untranslatable: An Operationalizable Ontology for Untranslatability

author.name: Jacob Bremerman, Brihi Joshi, Hirona Arai, Xiang Ren, Jonathan May

entry.summary: Introduces a structured ontology of untranslatability and a taxonomy of compensation strategies, operationalized into a multilingual dataset of untranslatable sentences with strategy-based translations. It enables controlled analysis of MT behavior on cases resisting one-to-one equivalence.

entry.title: AIPatient Arena: EHR-grounded evaluation of large language models in end-to-end clinical consultation workflows

author.name: Jiahui Niu, Huizi Yu, Wenkong Wang, Guangxin Dai, Jingxian He, Xiang Li, Zhiying Liang, Xinxin Lin, Kent CY So, Bryan YP Yan, Yun Kwok Wing, Yanqiu Xing, Xin Ma, Lizhou Fan

entry.summary: AIPatient Arena is an EHR-grounded evaluation framework assessing LLMs across eight dimensions of clinical competence using patient-specific knowledge graphs and multi-turn interactions. It is validated on a primary cohort and two out-of-distribution cohorts.

entry.title: Handling Feature Heterogeneity with Learnable Graph Patches

author.name: Yifei Sun, Yang Yang, Xiao Feng, Zijun Wang, Haoyang Zhong, Chunping Wang, Lei Chen

entry.summary: Proposes learnable graph patches as the smallest semantic units to address feature heterogeneity across graph datasets lacking textual information, enabling transferable graph foundation models. It decomposes graphs by unfolding node features and constructing corresponding patch structures.

entry.title: When AI Says "I have been in similar situations": Synthetic Lived Experience in Peer-Like Caregiver Support

author.name: Drishti Goel, Violeta J. Rodriguez, Daniel S. Brown, Ravi Karkar, Dong Whi Yoo, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: Examines the synthetic lived experience paradox when LLMs designed as peer-like caregiver support imply lived experiences they cannot authentically have. Highlights the tension between warmth/relatability and deceptive self-positioning in AI emotional support.

entry.title: CODEBLOCK: Learning to Supervise Code at the Right Granularity

author.name: Zhijie Deng, Ling Li, Jinlong Pang, Kaiqin Hu, Qi Xuan, Zhaowei Zhu, Jiaheng Wei

entry.summary: Proposes CodeBlock, a structure-aware sparse supervision framework for fine-tuning code LLMs that selects structure-complete code units rather than isolated tokens, avoiding the breakage that token-level masking causes for syntactically coherent code. Selects high-quality pairs then partitions code by structure.

entry.title: A Link between Shock-wave Theory and Symmetry-reduced Stochastic Gradient Descent for Artificial Neural Networks

author.name: Taiki Miyagawa

entry.summary: Develops a mathematically explicit link between shock-wave theory and symmetry-quotiented SGD dynamics, showing the effective dynamics satisfy a viscous Hamilton-Jacobi (Burgers-type) equation on the quotient manifold with rigorous shock formation. Applies the theory to MLPs, CNNs, and Transformers.

entry.title: Learning from Your Own Mistakes: Constructing Learnable Micro-Reflective Trajectories for Self-Distillation

author.name: Zhilin Huang, Hang Gao, Ziqiang Dong, Yuan Chen, Yifeng Luo, Chujun Qin, Jingyi Wang, Yang Yang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: TAPO advances self-distillation from implicit logit alignment to explicit correction by constructing learnable micro-reflective trajectories from the model's own mistakes. It provides fine-grained corrective guidance pinpointing where and why reasoning fails rather than imitating a privileged distribution.

entry.title: Quantifying and Auditing LLM Evaluation via Positive--Unlabeled Learning

author.name: Zilong Zhang, Yi-Ting Hung, Lei Ding, Chi-Kuang Yeh

entry.summary: This work formulates LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation under selective human supervision as a positive-unlabeled learning problem, using Partial Optimal Transport to audit and identify human-consistent preferences and detect biases like verbosity bias. It provides a geometric framework for auditing scalable LLM evaluation.

entry.title: VISUALSKILL: Multimodal Skills for Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Ziyan Jiang, Li An, Yujian Liu, Jiabao Ji, Qiucheng Wu, Jacob Andreas, Yang Zhang, Shiyu Chang

entry.summary: VISUALSKILL introduces hierarchical multimodal skills for computer-use agents that combine text and visual figures, consumed through an MCP tool that fetches relevant topic content on demand. It addresses the limitation that existing skill libraries represent GUI skills as text-only despite the visual nature of interaction.

entry.title: PreUnlearn: Auditing Collateral Knowledge Damage Before Large Language Model Unlearning

author.name: Bo Su, Ankit Shah, Thai Le

entry.summary: PreUnlearn studies how LLM unlearning effects propagate from the forget set to related and distant knowledge, finding a consistent decay pattern of collateral damage that weakens with semantic distance but persists across domains. It develops a method to audit potential collateral damage before unlearning is executed.

entry.title: Output Vector Editing for Memorization Mitigation in Large Language Models

author.name: Ahmad Dawar Hakimi, Kaiwei Lei, Isabelle Augenstein, Hinrich Sch\"utze

entry.summary: This work proposes output vector editing, a constrained-optimization weight edit that minimally modifies the output vectors of a few MLP neurons responsible for memorized continuations to redirect their residual-stream contributions. It argues output vectors, not activations, are what write memorized content, improving on activation-zeroing methods.

entry.title: GraphPO: Graph-based Policy Optimization for Reasoning Models

author.name: Yuliang Zhan, Xinyu Tang, Jian Li, Dandan Zheng, Weilong Chai, Jingdong Chen, Jun Zhou, Ge Wu, Wenyue Tang, Hao Sun

entry.summary: GraphPO is a graph-based policy optimization method for reasoning models that addresses redundant exploration of similar intermediate reasoning steps and sparse final-answer rewards in RLVR. It improves over tree-based methods which still expand branches independently even when reaching similar reasoning states.

entry.title: Neural Phase Correlation

author.name: Cole Reynolds

entry.summary: Introduces Neural Phase Correlation, a learned generalization of classical phase correlation that represents inter-image transformation as a first-class object by learning the decomposition basis, lifting the fixed-basis limit beyond global translation. Treats correspondence as inherently relational.

entry.title: APT: Atomic Physical Transitions for Causal Video-Language Understanding

author.name: Shang Wu, Haoran Lu, Songling Liu, Chenwei Xu, Lie Lu, Pranav Maneriker, Fan Du, Manling Li, Zhaoran Wang, Han Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Atomic Physical Transitions (APTs), representing videos as ordered causal state-change sequences rather than single event labels, to capture the physical mechanisms behind events. Constructs mixed-source data to make APT chains learnable by VLMs for causal video-language understanding.

entry.title: Moving Beyond Diversity: Visual Token Pruning as Subspace Reconstruction for Efficient VLMs

author.name: Jaeyeon Lee, Shunjie Wen, Dong-Wan Choi

entry.summary: Proposes SPARE, reformulating visual token pruning for VLMs as a column subset selection problem that minimizes reconstruction error, preserving magnitude information discarded by cosine-based diversity methods. Iteratively selects tokens with large projection residuals for better compositional reasoning.

entry.title: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Detecting AI-Generated Text-Rich Images from GPT-Image-2

author.name: Yijin Wang, Shuyi Wang, Wenhan Zhang, Yuqi Ouyang

entry.summary: Presents a multi-domain benchmark of 8,602 images across six categories for detecting AI-generated text-rich images produced by GPT-Image-2 (an existing model released in April 2026). It targets digital trust and content authenticity for layout- and text-centric synthetic imagery.

entry.title: Incumbent Advantage: Brand Bias and Cognitive Manipulation Dynamics in LLM Recommendation Systems

author.name: Xi Chu, Yupeng Hou

entry.summary: Examines brand bias in LLM product recommendations, finding well-known brands dominate when specs are equal but lose advantage with tiny competitor rating gains. Tests across GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet, and Gemini-3-Flash on skincare products.

entry.title: Closing the Feedback Loop: From Experience Extraction to Insight Governance in Verbal Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yanwei Cui, Xing Zhang, Yulong Zhang, Li Shao, Xiaofeng Shi, Guanghui Wang, Peiyang He

entry.summary: Proposes a governance framework for verbal reinforcement learning that manages the retention-forgetting dilemma in non-stationary environments through outcome-driven evaluation and a non-monotonic knowledge lifecycle. It governs which verbal insights agents keep or discard.

entry.title: LongWebBench: Evaluating Structural and Functional Webpage Generation in Long-Horizon Settings

author.name: Yi Zhao, Zhen Yang, Mengpan Chen, Mingde Xu, Shanghui Gong, Xijun Liu, Jibing Gong, Jie Tang

entry.summary: Introduces LongWebBench for evaluating long-horizon webpage generation from visual inputs, with 490 long webpages for structural fidelity and 507 interaction tasks for functional verification. It combines VLM-based and DOM-augmented agent protocols.

entry.title: DriveJudge: Rethinking Autonomous Driving Evaluation with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xinglong Sun, Kevin Xie, Jenny Schmalfuss, Despoina Paschalidou, Xiuming Zhang, Sanja Fidler, Kashyap Chitta, Jose M. Alvarez

entry.summary: DriveJudge is an autonomous driving evaluation agent that combines rule-grounded evaluation with vision-language model reasoning, selectively invoking physically-grounded rule functions after interpreting context. It aims for evaluation that is both interpretable and context-aware.

entry.title: NarrativeWorldBench: A Frontier-Saturated Benchmark and a Latent World Model for Long-Horizon Co-Creative Audio Drama

author.name: Logan Mann, Abdur Rahman, Mohammad Saifullah, Taaha Kazi, Vasu Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces NarrativeWorldBench, an open benchmark of nine narrative-structure metrics across horizons for long-form serialized audio drama, plus a Narrative Variational State-Space Model. It shows all closed-frontier LLMs saturate and collapse at long horizons across four Indic languages.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Post-Hoc Uncertainty Quantification in Operator Learning

author.name: Oriol Vendrell-Gallart, Nima Negarandeh, Ramin Bostanabad

entry.summary: REEF-GP is a post-hoc uncertainty quantification framework for neural operators that fits a Gaussian process to residuals using the operator's internal embeddings as the kernel feature space. It produces geometry-aware uncertainties under geometric variability in PDE surrogates.

entry.title: OmniDrive: An LLM-Choreographed Multi-Agent World Model with Unified Latent Co-Compression for Multi-View Driving Video Generation

author.name: Zijie Meng, Yufei Liu, Chengqian Ma, Zhiyu Li, Jiyuan Liu, Wenhua Nie, Bingcai Wei, Shuqin Chen, Weichen Xu, Jiquan Yuan, Miao Zhang

entry.summary: OmniDrive (DRIVE-CHOREO) is an LLM-choreographed multi-agent world model that recasts controllable multi-view driving video generation as latent choreography with a shared symbolic interlingua. Three Qwen2.5-VL agents handle directing, mapping, and generation to align language, geometry, and pixels.

entry.title: ASTEROID: A Spatiotemporal Information Transformer for Forecasting Multi-Step Time Series of Molecular Dynamics

author.name: Kexin Wu, Luonan Chen, Renxiao Wang

entry.summary: ASTEROID is a spatiotemporal transformer that directly predicts multi-step atomic coordinates for molecular dynamics, avoiding iterative integration by reformulating trajectories as high-dimensional spatiotemporal sequences. It integrates a Spatiotemporal Information Transformation equation into the architecture.

entry.title: Dimensionality Controls When Modularity Helps in Continual Learning

author.name: Kathrin Korte, Christian Medeiros Adriano, Joachim Winther Pedersen, Eleni Nisioti, Sebastian Risi

entry.summary: Investigates how modular architecture, task similarity, and representational dimensionality jointly shape continual learning in an A-B-A paradigm. Finds that modularity matters mainly in low-dimensional regimes, with little benefit in high-dimensional lazy regimes.

entry.title: EAGG: Embodiment-Aligned Grasp Generation via Geometry-Aware Graph Conditioning

author.name: Wanhao Niu, Qiyan Ke, Yuan Sun, Hao Sun, Jie Xu, Muyuan Ma, Ruiqi Hu, Fuchun Sun

entry.summary: Presents EAGG, an embodiment-aligned grasp generator that represents each end-effector with a topology-aware graph and low-dimensional control space for cross-embodiment grasp generation. Aims to generalize across parallel grippers and dexterous hands.

entry.title: Kolmogorov Regression for Robust Diffusion Policies

author.name: Lekan Molu

entry.summary: Introduces Kolmogorov regression, lifting finite-dimensional diffusion policies to a Cameron-Martin Hilbert space via a backward Kolmogorov PDE to reduce temporal drift from discretization artifacts in robot control. Uses Gaussian measure theory and a precision-weighted loss for robustness.

entry.title: The Illusion of Improvement: Reject Inference Strategies in Credit Scoring

author.name: Bruno Scarone, Ricardo Baeza-Yates

entry.summary: Reveals a structural failure of reject inference methods in credit scoring where accuracy improves while recall collapses, creating an illusion of improvement while rejection quality deteriorates. It proposes deliberately approving a fraction of rejected applicants to break the feedback loop without statistical assumptions.

entry.title: Do as the Romans Do: Learning Universal Behaviors from Heterogeneous Agents

author.name: Caleb Chang, Davin Win Kyi, Natasha Jaques, Karen Leung

entry.summary: GRID is a social learning method that extracts universally useful behaviors from heterogeneous demonstrators by decomposing per-agent rewards into a shared general reward and agent-specific rewards. Training on the general reward yields behaviors transferable across the population.

entry.title: PACT: Preserving Anchored Cores in Task-vectors for Model Merging

author.name: Ningyuan Shi, Zhipeng Zhou, Hao Wang, Chunyan Miao, Peilin Zhao

entry.summary: PACT improves model merging by identifying Load-Bearing Wall dimensions, task-critical knowledge encoded in pretrained parameters rather than task vectors, and preserving them during merging. It challenges the assumption that all task knowledge lives in task vectors.

entry.title: Contextualizing Biological Language Models across Modalities via Logit-Space Contrastive Alignment

author.name: Yanjun Shao, Yundi Chen, Yashvi Patel, Aurelien Pelissier, Mar\'ia Rodr\'iguez Mart\'inez

entry.summary: LOGICA performs context-conditioned prediction for biological language models via contrastive alignment directly in logit space, preserving the per-token probability interface used for sequence design and variant scoring. It avoids distorting outputs through pooled embeddings or task-specific heads.

entry.title: Private Learning with Public Feature Conditioning

author.name: Shuli Jiang, Walid Krichene, Nicolas Mayoraz

entry.summary: Cond-DP is a conditioned variant of DP-SGD for differentially private regression that exploits public, non-sensitive feature structure with a data-driven conditioning matrix to accelerate convergence. It addresses the underexplored semi-sensitive-feature regression setting common in recommendation and advertising.

entry.title: Anomaly Detection for Sparse and Irregular Multivariate Time Series with Latent SDEs

author.name: Martin Uray, Dominik Geng, Florian Graf, Stefan Huber, Roland Kwitt

entry.summary: Proposes a generative latent SDE approach for multivariate time series anomaly detection that handles sparse, irregularly sampled, and partially observed data by projecting observations onto a continuous-time stochastic dynamical system. It ranks first among state-of-the-art baselines on six benchmarks.

entry.title: OpenAnt: LLM-Powered Vulnerability Discovery Through Code Decomposition, Adversarial Verification, and Dynamic Testing

author.name: Nahum Korda, Gadi Evron

entry.summary: OpenAnt is an open-source LLM-powered vulnerability discovery system integrating static analysis with LLM reasoning through code decomposition, adversarial verification, and dynamic testing. It addresses high false-positive rates in static analysis and infrastructure costs of fuzzing for repository-scale security.

entry.title: Optimal scenario design for climate emulation

author.name: Christopher B. Womack, Shahine Bouabid, Andrei Sokolov, Popat Salunke, Glenn Flierl, Sebastian D. Eastham, Noelle E. Selin

entry.summary: This work shows that low structural diversity in standard climate scenarios limits ML climate emulator generalization, and introduces a method using a differentiable Simple Climate Model to optimize training datasets for better extrapolation to novel scenarios. It shifts focus from architecture design to optimizing training data structure.

entry.title: Continuous Audio Thinking for Large Audio Language Models

author.name: Gyojin Han, Dong-Jae Lee, Changho Choi, Jongsuk Kim, Junmo Kim

entry.summary: Continuous Audio Thinking (CoAT) equips large audio language models with a continuous latent workspace to organize acoustic information like prosody, affect, and pitch before generating text responses. It addresses how LALMs lose acoustic detail because their hidden states are shaped for text generation.

entry.title: Are LLMs Ready to Assist Physicians? PhysAssistBench for Interactive Doctor-Patient-EHR Assistance

author.name: Tianming Du, Peijie Yu, Sihan Shang, Danli Shi, My Linh Nguyen, Shengbo Gao, Guangyuan Li, Yinghong Yu, Yan Jiang, Qianlong Zhao, Behzad Bozorgtabar, Shaoxiong Ji, Jiazhen Pan, Daniel Rueckert, Jiancheng Yang

entry.summary: PhysAssistBench is a benchmark for interactive doctor-patient-EHR assistance built from real MIMIC-IV cases, using agentic patients that turn static records into multi-turn clinical scenarios. It evaluates whether medical LLMs can coordinate clinical knowledge, EHR tool use, and patient communication in the same interaction.

entry.title: Enhancing Decision-Making with Large Language Models through Multi-Agent Fictitious Play

author.name: Leyang Shen, Yang Zhang, Xiaoyan Zhao, Chun Kai Ling, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Proposes Multi-Agent Fictitious Play (MAFP), representing stakeholder stances as agents to handle decision-making tasks with mutually-dependent stances, which the authors term stance entanglement. Distinguishes this decision complexity from execution complexity in multi-agent systems.

entry.title: Decoupling Search from Reasoning: A Vendor-Agnostic Grounding Architecture for LLM Agents

author.name: Emmanuel Aboah Boateng, Kyle MacDonald, Amardeep Kumar, Siddharth Kodwani, Sudeep Das

entry.summary: Proposes Decoupled Search Grounding (DSG), a vendor-agnostic architecture moving retrieval grounding outside the reasoning model via an MCP-compatible gateway, exposing routing, caching, and context rendering as first-class controls. Addresses search-induced verbosity and coupling in production LLM agents.

entry.title: Hallucination Detection and Correction in Medical VLMs via Counter-Evidence Verification

author.name: Nan Zhou, Ke Zou, Meng Liu, Linchao He, Jiaqi Zhu, Yi Zhang, Hu Chen, Huazhu Fu

entry.summary: Proposes CoEV, a training-free framework for detecting and correcting hallucinations in medical VLMs through bidirectional counter-evidence verification between textual assertions and visual evidence. Goes beyond attention analysis to verify whether attention reflects supporting evidence.

entry.title: URDF Synthesis from RGB-D Sequences via Differentiable Joint Inference and Energy-Consistent Verification

author.name: Xinze Zhang

entry.summary: Presents KinemaForge, a constraint-driven pipeline jointly inferring part shape, joint topology, and joint parameters of articulated objects from short RGB-D sequences, validated against an energy-consistent differentiable rigid-body dynamics verifier. Produces simulation-ready URDF digital twins that respect dynamic invariants.

entry.title: BindEdit: Taming Attention Leakage for Precise Multi-Object Image Editing

author.name: Chaewon Park, Soyoon Lee, Naeun Lee, Minjung Shin, Seogkyu Jeon, Kibeom Hong

entry.summary: Proposes BindEdit, addressing attention leakage in multi-object image editing by identifying edit-token leakage and source-dominance leakage and enforcing attention-level constraints within a single diffusion trajectory. Reduces semantic blending, object duplication, and incomplete edits.

entry.title: AMALIA-VL: A Native European Portuguese Open-Source Vision and Language Model

author.name: Diogo Gl\'oria-Silva, Jo\~ao Cardeira, Manuel Letras da Luz, Afonso Simpl\'icio, Gon\c{c}alo Vinagre, Diogo Tavares, Rafael Ferreira, In\^es Calvo, In\^es Vieira, David Semedo, Jo\~ao Magalh\~aes

entry.summary: AMALIA-VL is the first open-source instruction-tuned vision-language model built natively for European Portuguese, with a three-stage training pipeline and a pt-PT-centric multimodal data mix. It addresses systematic underrepresentation of pt-PT in multimodal models.

entry.title: Benchmarking Action Spaces in Reinforcement Learning for Vision-based Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Seyed Alireza Azimi, Homayoon Farrahi, Abhishek Naik, Colin Bellinger, A. Rupam Mahmood

entry.summary: Benchmarks four action-space representations (pose increment, pose velocity, joint position increment, joint velocity) across vision-based picking and pushing in sim-to-real RL, finding joint velocity best for smoothness and task performance. It offers practical guidance for action-space choice.

entry.title: Monocular 3D Occupancy Perception for Robots on Sidewalks via Hybrid 2D-3D Learning

author.name: Yukai Ma, Joe Lin, Liu Liu, Honglin He, Lulu Ricketts, Brad Squicciarini, Yong Liu, Bolei Zhou

entry.summary: WalkOCC is a hybrid ray-marching monocular 3D occupancy perception framework for sidewalk robots that couples LiDAR-RGB geometric grounding with scalable learning from large unlabeled data. It targets cluttered, unstructured sidewalks underserved by on-road occupancy pipelines.

entry.title: Beyond Parallel Sampling: Diverse Query Initialization for Agentic Search

author.name: Sidhaarth Murali, Jo\~ao Coelho, Jingjie Ning, Jo\~ao Magalh\~aes, Bruno Martins, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: Proposes DivInit, a training-free method that diversifies the first query in agentic search to overcome diminishing returns from parallel sampling caused by query redundancy. By selecting diverse seed queries, it reduces overlapping retrieval and improves breadth scaling across open-weight models.

entry.title: Can LLMs Be CEOs? Benchmarking Strategic Resource Reallocation with Multi-Role Agent Simulation

author.name: Yuyang Dai, Xueqing Peng, Lingfei Qian, Zhuohan Xie

entry.summary: Introduces CEO-Bench, a multi-agent benchmark evaluating LLMs on executive strategic resource reallocation under conflicting stakeholder input, information asymmetry, and organizational constraints. It moves beyond isolated cognitive task evaluation.

entry.title: EComAgentBench: Benchmarking Shopping Agents on Long-Horizon Tasks with Distributed Hidden Intent

author.name: Zeyao Du, Tong Li, Haibo Zhang

entry.summary: Presents EComAgentBench, a benchmark of 662 tasks grounded in real Amazon products where shopper requirements are scattered across query, profile, and clarification. It tests whether agents uncover hidden intent over long horizons and verify candidates against evidence.

entry.title: Trust the Right Teacher: Quality-Aware Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding

author.name: Jingyuan Huang, Zuming Huang, Yucheng Shi, Tianze Yang, Xiaoming Zhai, Wei Chu, Ninghao Liu

entry.summary: Proposes quality-aware self-distillation for VLM-based GUI grounding, addressing unreliable teacher signals when student-generated prefixes deviate from target coordinates. It improves coordinate-sensitive grounding in high-resolution screenshots.

entry.title: Do Large Language Models Always Tell The Same Stories?

author.name: Thennal DK, Hans Ole Hatzel

entry.summary: Investigates the diversity of LLM-generated stories using narrative similarity judgments across 10 models with human and automatic evaluation. It finds LLM narratives are consistently more similar to each other than human-written stories are.

entry.title: Enhancing Pathological VLMs with Cross-scale Reasoning

author.name: Chi Phan, Tianyi Zhang, Qiaochu Xue, Yufeng Wu, Dan Hu, Zeyu Liu, Sudong Wang, Yueming Jin

entry.summary: Introduces the first cross-scale training and evaluation paradigm for pathology VLMs, formulating interpretation as multi-magnification reasoning that integrates global architecture and cellular morphology. It addresses the lack of explicit cross-scale reasoning objectives in existing datasets.

entry.title: Scaling Enterprise Agent Routing: Degradation, Diagnosis, and Recovery

author.name: Kellen Gillespie, Robyn Perry

entry.summary: Studies how enterprise agent routing accuracy degrades as the tool catalog scales from 10 to 110 agents and 584 tools, decomposing degradation into retrieval and confusion gaps. It shows embedding-based shortlisting recovers significant F1 across frontier models.

entry.title: MIVE: A Minimalist Integer Vector Engine for Softmax LayerNorm and RMSNorm Acceleration

author.name: Kosmas Alexandridis, Giorgos Dimitrakopoulos

entry.summary: Introduces MIVE, a programmable integer vector engine that executes Softmax, LayerNorm, and RMSNorm within a unified datapath rather than separate hardware blocks. Targets reducing silicon waste in LLM inference accelerators.

entry.title: The Measurement Gap in the Automation of EU Law: Benchmarking Doctrinal Legal Reasoning under the EU AI Act

author.name: Mich\`ele Finck

entry.summary: A legal scholarship piece arguing there is a measurement gap in legal AI: no benchmark evaluates whether LLMs perform doctrinal legal reasoning, while the EU AI Act mandates appropriate accuracy for high-risk judicial AI. Frames this gap as both methodological and legally consequential.

entry.title: Fisher Width: A Geometric Measure of Complexity on Statistical Manifolds

author.name: Vu Khac Ky

entry.summary: Introduces Fisher width, a Fisher-geometric analogue of Gaussian width for statistical manifolds, scaling directions by statistical distinguishability rather than Euclidean length. Extends a central complexity measure from high-dimensional probability to Riemannian statistical geometry.

entry.title: ThousandWorlds: A benchmark for climate emulation of potentially habitable exoplanets

author.name: Edward T. Stevenson, Mei Ting Mak, Eric Wolf, Denis E. Sergeev, Tobi Hammond, N. J. Mayne, Miles Cranmer

entry.summary: ThousandWorlds is an ML-ready benchmark for emulating exoplanet climate models, curating a multi-model dataset to replace expensive global climate model runs with learned emulators. It targets low-data, multi-simulator parameter-to-field regression for assessing habitability signatures.

entry.title: Signature filtering: a lightweight enhancement for statistical watermark detection in large language models

author.name: Chih-Duo Hong, Yen-Pang Chen, Fang Yu

entry.summary: Proposes signature filtering, a detection-time module that identifies and removes 'signature' tokens that make statistical watermark tests unreliable, improving LLM watermark detection without changing embedding. It solves a mixed-integer program to maximize true positive rate and derives statistical bounds against several attacker models.

entry.title: Effects of sparsity and superposition on loss in simple autoencoders

author.name: Mriganka Basu Roy Chowdhury, Eric McLaughlin Weiner

entry.summary: Extends the Elhage et al. toy model analysis of superposition, deriving how sparsity and superposition affect loss in simple autoencoders. It provides additional theoretical understanding of polysemanticity and feature compression in low-dimensional representations.

entry.title: Robust and Interpretable Adaptation of Equivariant Materials Foundation Models via Sparsity-promoting Fine-tuning

author.name: Youngwoo Cho, Seunghoon Yi, Wooil Yang, Sungmo Kang, Young-woo Son, Jaegul Choo, Joonseok Lee, Soo Kyung Kim, Hongkee Yoon

entry.summary: Proposes a sparsity-promoting fine-tuning method for E(3)-equivariant materials foundation models that selectively updates parameters by exploiting their structural properties. It matches or exceeds full and low-rank fine-tuning on energy and force prediction across molecular and crystalline benchmarks.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Foundation Models Should Already Be A Thing

author.name: Abdelrahman Zighem, Jill-J\^enn Vie

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that reinforcement learning foundation models should already exist, drawing analogy to TabPFN-style synthetic-prior pretraining for tabular tasks. It contends sampling synthetic MDPs is as feasible as synthetic tabular datasets and that MDPs admit fixed-size sufficient statistics for in-context RL.

entry.title: Sequential Kernel-based Conditional Independence Testing via Adaptive Betting

author.name: Zheng He, Danica J. Sutherland

entry.summary: This paper presents a sequential kernel-based conditional independence test using testing-by-betting that is robust to estimation errors in the Model-X conditional distribution. It addresses the fragility of existing sequential tests that require exact conditional knowledge.

entry.title: Freeing the Law with LOCUS: A Local Ordinance Corpus for the United States

author.name: Denis Peskoff, Joe Barrow, Christopher Vu, Diag Davenport

entry.summary: LOCUS is a comprehensive, county-harmonized corpus of US local ordinance codes, filling a major gap in machine-readable legal text that governs zoning, housing, and everyday regulation. It provides researchers bulk access to fragmented local law previously locked in vendor browsing platforms.

entry.title: LLM Parameters for Math Across Languages: Shared or Separate?

author.name: Behzad Shomali, Luisa Victor, Tim Selbach, Ali Hamza Bashir, David Berghaus, Joachim Koehler, Mehdi Ali, Markus Frey

entry.summary: This mechanistic analysis localizes and compares LLM parameters supporting mathematical reasoning across languages, finding partial cross-lingual overlap concentrated in intermediate layers with English producing the largest parameter set. It clarifies whether cross-lingual math performance differences reflect shared or separate mechanisms.

entry.title: PragReST: Self-Reinforcing Counterfactual Reasoning for Pragmatic Language Understanding

author.name: Jihyung Park, Minchao Huang, Leqi Liu, Elias Stengel-Eskin

entry.summary: PragReST is a self-supervised framework for improving LLM pragmatic reasoning by constructing pragmatic QA data, generating counterfactual reasoning traces, and training via SFT and RL without human labels or teacher distillation. It addresses LLMs' tendency to choose literal over implied interpretations.

entry.title: RegMix-D: Dynamic Data Mixing via Proxy Training Trajectories

author.name: Kaiyan Zhao, Zhongtao Miao, Akiko Aizawa, Yoshimasa Tsuruoka

entry.summary: RegMix-D extends RegMix for LLM pretraining data mixture selection by using full loss trajectories from proxy runs rather than only endpoint losses, enabling dynamic mixture schedules. It supports offline complete schedules and online adaptive mixing during training.

entry.title: LegalWorld: A Life-Cycle Interactive Environment for Legal Agents

author.name: Songhan Zuo, Shengbin Yue, Tao Chiang, Guanying Li, Yun Song, Xuanjing Huang, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: LegalWorld is a life-cycle interactive environment modeling Chinese civil litigation as a causally connected chain of five stages grounded in over 75,000 paired judgments, where early decisions constrain later outcomes. It addresses the limitation that prior legal simulators reinitialize each scenario without cross-stage causal dependencies.

entry.title: Leadership as Coordination Control: Behavioral Signatures and the Recovery-Advantage Boundary in Multi-Agent LLM Teams

author.name: Haewoon Kwak

entry.summary: Investigates when process-level leadership/coordination control adds value in multi-agent LLM teams, operationalizing classical leadership styles as explicit action-set controllers. Uses behavioral signatures and ablations to map a recovery-advantage boundary.

entry.title: RegimeVGGT: Layer-Wise Spatially Preserving Redundancy Removal for Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer

author.name: Jinhao You (University of Pennsylvania), Shuo Lyu (University of Pennsylvania), Zhuohang Lyu (University of Pennsylvania), Tanxuan Li (University of Pennsylvania), Zibo Zhao (University of Pennsylvania), Jiaxiang Hu (University of California, Irvine), Kai Tang (Nanyang Technological University), Yichen Guo (Nanyang Technological University)

entry.summary: Proposes RegimeVGGT, a training-free layer-wise compression method for Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer based on spectral/probing/causal analysis revealing three layer regimes. Applies U-shaped compression protecting geometry-salient tokens and pose-relevant attention.

entry.title: Show, Don't Ask: Generative Visual Disambiguation for Composed Image Retrieval with Turn-Valid Coverage

author.name: Amsisan Tran, Baogh Le, Tuan Kiet Pham, Sui Yang Guang

entry.summary: Presents CLARA, a composed image retrieval clarification framework that resolves query ambiguity by showing users visual alternatives rather than asking text questions, with coverage guarantees extended beyond the first interaction. It targets fine-grained visual differences that text clarification cannot capture.

entry.title: Sensor Configuration Matters: A Systematic Evaluation of Multimodal SLAM on Quadruped Robots

author.name: Roberto Corlito, Fabian Schmidt, Nils Seibert, Markus Enzweiler, Abhinav Valada, Arne Roennau

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates how hardware-level sensor configurations affect visual, visual-inertial, and LiDAR-visual-inertial SLAM under the aggressive dynamics of quadruped locomotion. It highlights embodiment-induced challenges like foot-impact shocks and high-frequency vibrations.

entry.title: As You Wish: Mission Planning with Formal Verification using LLMs in Precision Agriculture

author.name: Marcos Abel Zuzu\'arregui, Stefano Carpin

entry.summary: Extends an LLM-based precision agriculture mission planner with multiple feedback loops using linear temporal logic to formally verify that natural-language-specified plans meet requirements. It addresses the inherent ambiguity of natural language in robot mission specification.

entry.title: Guardian Angels: LLM Personalization for Productivity and Security

author.name: gwern

entry.summary: Gwern proposes 'Guardian Angels': personalized digital-twin LLMs that emulate an individual's personality, values, and preferences rather than acting as generic assistants, thereby weakly resolving the principal-agent problem by unifying principal and agent. Such GAs would handle productivity, cybersecurity, and cognitive-security screening against synthetic-media attacks.

entry.title: A Machine-Learned Comorbidity Index

author.name: Suleman Baloch, Kishlay Jha, Alberto M. Segre, Philip M. Polgreen, Bijaya Adhikari

entry.summary: Proposes a Machine-Learned Comorbidity Index that maps diagnosis codes to a single scalar by maximizing nHSIC dependence with multiple clinical outcomes. It captures nonlinear, outcome-specific risk beyond mortality-centric scores like Charlson.

entry.title: DeepInsight: A Unified Evaluation Infrastructure Across the Physical AI Stack

author.name: Siyi Li, Chunyu Sun, Jiahao Zhang, Yuchen Kang, Wuliang Wang, Yu Qiu, Rui Jiang, Haitao Cui, Jie Chen

entry.summary: Presents DeepInsight, a unified evaluation infrastructure spanning the full physical AI stack from foundation-model decoding to whole-body control on a single runtime. It preserves regime heterogeneity behind narrow abstractions to diagnose cross-layer regressions.

entry.title: Probing, Fusion, and Trustworthiness: A Systematic Evaluation of Foundation Model Representations for Multimodal Cancer Analysis

author.name: Jingyu Hu, Giuseppe Tripodi, Reed Naidoo, Sarah F. McGough, Tapabrata Chakraborti

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates foundation model representations for multimodal cancer analysis across whole-slide images and transcriptomic profiles on commercial oncology cohorts. It examines unimodal probing, multimodal fusion, and trustworthiness under distribution shift.

entry.title: LLM Features Can Hurt GNNs: Concatenation Interference on Homophilous Graph Benchmarks

author.name: Zhongyuan Wang, Pratyusha Vemuri

entry.summary: Documents that adding LLM-generated node features to GNNs via pure input concatenation can systematically degrade accuracy on homophilous benchmarks, contrary to common reports. The drop attenuates when relaxing conditions like backbone choice and integration method.

entry.title: ReAge3D: Re-Aging 3D Faces with View Consistency

author.name: Libing Zeng, Li Ma, Mingming He, Ning Yu, Paul Debevec, Nima Khademi Kalantari

entry.summary: Presents ReAge3D for realistic, identity-preserving, view-consistent 3D face re-aging, using a 2D diffusion re-aging model and a center-out editing propagation strategy to avoid over-smoothing age details across views. Addresses inconsistencies that degrade subtle age-related details in 3D editing.

entry.title: SAGE: Retain-Aware Post-Hoc Sanitization of Final Unlearning Vector

author.name: Jingyuan Zhang, Yucheng Bai, Peixi Wen, Zhehao Huang, Zhengbao He, Hanling Tian, Xinwen Cheng, Haiyin Ran, Xiaolin Huang

entry.summary: Presents Artemis, an anatomy-resolved causal intervention framework that removes demographic confounders (age, sex) from multimodal neuroimaging GNN analysis of fMRI and DTI brain networks. Incorporates real-world clinical confounders rather than domain-agnostic causal mechanisms.

entry.title: TS-Fault: Benchmarking Time Series Forecasters Against Structural Faults

author.name: Yuyang Zhao, Lian Xu, Hao Miao, Chenxi Liu, Hao Xue

entry.summary: TS-Fault is a benchmark that evaluates time series forecasters under explicit, parameterized structural fault scenarios such as broken cross-variable dependencies and regime change with missingness. It reframes forecasting robustness as a data-quality problem with controllable semantic difficulty.

entry.title: InTrain: Intrinsic Trainability for Zero-Cost Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Qinqin Zhou, Fuhai Chen, Jipeng Wu, Zhiwei Chen, Zhikai Hu, Weiwei Cai

entry.summary: InTrain introduces a unified theoretical proxy for zero-cost neural architecture search that formalizes trainability via geometric capacity and optimization resilience. It replaces fragmented heuristics with a principled architectural invariant quantified through activation covariance spectra.

entry.title: Bayesian Anytime Pareto Set Identification for Multi-Objective Multi-Armed Bandits

author.name: Lennert Saerens, Bram Silue, Eleni Litsa, Peter Vrancx, Pieter Libin

entry.summary: Introduces TTPFTS, the first anytime multi-objective multi-armed bandit algorithm for Pareto set identification, taking a Bayesian Top-Two Thompson Sampling approach with a novel uncertainty quantification metric. It is demonstrated on synthetic environments and ultra-large molecular discovery libraries.

entry.title: Wasserstein Policy Learning for Distributional Outcomes

author.name: Yiyan Huang, Cheuk Hang Leung, Qi Wu, Zhiheng Zhang

entry.summary: This work studies offline policy learning where outcomes are probability distributions rather than scalars, defining rewards through utility functionals on Wasserstein barycenters and establishing statistical guarantees with IPW and doubly-robust estimators. It extends individualized treatment rules to distributional outcomes.

entry.title: IndicContextEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Context Utilisation in Audio Large Language Models Across 8 Indic Languages

author.name: Sakshi Joshi, Dhruv Subhash Rathi, Sanskar Singh, Eldho Ittan George, R J Hari, Kaushal Bhogale, Mitesh M. Khapra

entry.summary: Introduces IndicContextEval, a 56-hour benchmark across 8 Indian languages and 23 domains with a 7-level prompting framework to test whether AudioLLMs genuinely use textual context versus relying on parametric knowledge. Reveals gaps in context utilisation.

entry.title: SP-TransientBench: A Real-Captured Single Photon Perception Benchmark

author.name: Hongzhou Dong, Zili Zhang, Ziting Wen, Yiheng Qiang, Runrong Deng, Wenle Dong, Ziwen Jiang, Xinyang Li, Rui Lu, Shuoyao Sun, Wenyu Wang, Ziyi Xia, Haitao Zheng, Guodong Shi, Xiaoqiang Ren

entry.summary: Introduces SP-TransientBench, a real-captured single-photon LiDAR perception benchmark covering depth estimation, multi-view reconstruction, and 3D semantic understanding under photon-starved conditions. Addresses the field's reliance on simulated or small-scale controlled data.

entry.title: DVANet: Degradation-aware Visual-prior Alignment Network for Image Restoration

author.name: Yanjie Tu, Qingsen Yan, Axi Niu, Tao Hu, Haokui Zhang, Jiantao Zhou

entry.summary: DVANet is a degradation-aware deep unfolding network for all-in-one image restoration that aligns visual priors to varied degradation types, aiming for interpretable iterative modeling. It addresses adaptability to complex and locally damaged content.

entry.title: A Scalable Embodied Intelligence Platform for Seamless Real-to-Sim-to-Real Transfer of Household Mobile Manipulation Tasks

author.name: Kui Yang, Xianlei Long, Haoxuan Li, Yan Ding, Chao Chen

entry.summary: BestMan is a scalable real-to-sim-to-real platform for household mobile manipulation that bridges high-fidelity scene reconstruction, systematic simulation evaluation, and real-world deployment. It aims to streamline strategy development across the full transfer cycle.

entry.title: Two-Phase Bilevel Search for the Moving-Target Traveling Salesman Problem with Moving Obstacles

author.name: Allen George Philip, Anoop Bhat, Sivakumar Rathinam, Howie Choset

entry.summary: Studies the Moving-Target Traveling Salesman Problem with Moving Obstacles, presenting a mixed-integer conic programming formulation and a fast two-phase bilevel search algorithm for high-quality feasible solutions. It generalizes MT-TSP to dynamic obstacle avoidance.

entry.title: Viking Hill Dataset: A Lidar-Radar-Camera Dataset for Detection and Segmentation in Forest Scenes

author.name: Vladim\'ir Kubelka, Oleksandr Kotlyar, Unal Artan, Martin Magnusson

entry.summary: Introduces the Viking Hill multi-sensor forest dataset with co-registered 4D imaging radar alongside LiDAR, RGB, IMU, and RTK-GNSS, with per-tree cuboid and diameter annotations across two contrasting vegetation states. It uniquely adds imaging radar, valued for resilience to visual degradation.

entry.title: In game theory, generalists sometimes win out over specialists

author.name: Steve Nadis | MIT Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems

entry.summary: MIT-led work presented at ICLR offers new theoretical insights into two-player zero-sum imperfect-information games, examining when generalist strategies outperform specialist ones. It contributes to the game-theory understanding of strategic decision-making under uncertainty like poker or bidding wars.

entry.title: Surrogate Assisted Pedestrian Protection Design via a Foundation Model Orchestrated Workflow

author.name: Osamu Ito, Akihiko Katagiri, Yoshikazu Nakagawa, Shin Saeki, Jun Shiraishi, Masato Sasaki

entry.summary: Presents the first foundation-model-orchestrated workflow for crash safety design, using surrogate models to predict pedestrian leg injury metrics and reduce evaluation time from hours to seconds. It tackles highly nonlinear crash dynamics difficult for surrogates.

entry.title: FinAcumen: Financial Multimodal Reasoning via Self-Evolving Experience Memory Harness

author.name: Pianran Guo, Pengcheng Zhou, Yucheng Jian, Shuhua Chen

entry.summary: Presents FinAcumen, a financial multimodal reasoning agent with selective experience memory that accumulates grounded reasoning experience from prior trajectories. It distills successful strategies to reduce hallucination and improve tool routing.

entry.title: Model Validation of Agentic AI Systems: A POMDP-Based Framework for Belief-State, Forecast, and Policy Validation

author.name: Matthew Francis Dixon

entry.summary: Proposes a POMDP-based model validation framework for agentic AI that decomposes autonomous decision-making into beliefs, forecasts, actions, and utility for independent validation. It addresses the new class of model risk introduced by autonomous agents beyond predictive accuracy.

entry.title: Feynman Kac Reweighted Schr\"odinger Bridge Matching for Surface-Based Tau PET Harmonization

author.name: Jianwei Zhang, Xinyu Nie, Jiaxin Yue, Yonggang Shi

entry.summary: FKRSBM is a Feynman-Kac reweighted Schrodinger Bridge Matching model for harmonizing Tau PET imaging across scanners and protocols while preserving biological signal. It addresses subgroup composition differences that risk conflating site effects with biological variation.

entry.title: TuneAhead: Predicting Fine-tuning Performance Before Full Training Begins

author.name: Yuxiang Luo, Haonan Long, Chen Wang, Qiqi Duan, Xiaotian Lin, Yanwei Xu, Yuyu Luo, Weikai Yang, Nan Tang

entry.summary: TuneAhead is a lightweight framework for pre-hoc prediction of LLM fine-tuning performance, encoding each run as a meta-feature vector combining static dataset descriptors with dynamic probe features. SHAP-based attributions provide interpretable diagnostics of which features drive predictions.

entry.title: Non-negative Elastic Net Decoding for Information Retrieval

author.name: Koki Okajima, Yasutoshi Ida, Tsukasa Yoshida, Yasuaki Nakamura

entry.summary: Reformulates dense retrieval as a joint decoding problem using non-negative elastic net optimization so that document selection considers the whole corpus context, reducing redundancy. Aims to retrieve more diverse, less redundant document sets.

entry.title: S4oP: Operator-level Pruning of Structured State Space Models for Resource-Constrained Devices

author.name: Marco Deano, Filippo Ziche, Nicola Bombieri

entry.summary: Proposes S4oP, the first systematic operator-level structured pruning approach for S4 and S4D state space models to reduce inference cost while preserving accuracy on resource-constrained devices. Progressively prunes operators incrementally.

entry.title: Bounded Context Management for Tabular Foundation Models on Stream Learning

author.name: Jinmo Lee, Doyun Choi, Moongi Choi, Jaemin Yoo

entry.summary: Proposes CURE, a context management policy for tabular foundation models in stream learning that preserves recent examples, retains uncertain ones, and removes redundant ones under bounded context. It reframes stream adaptation from updating model state to managing in-context examples.

entry.title: OneCanvas: 3D Scene Understanding via Panoramic Reprojection

author.name: Bart{\l}omiej Baranowski, Dave Zhenyu Chen, Matthias Nie{\ss}ner

entry.summary: OneCanvas performs 3D scene understanding in Vision-Language Models by aggregating patch features from all views onto a single equirectangular panoramic canvas using depth and camera pose, avoiding complex geometry encoders. A 3D position embedding restores depth information lost in the angular projection.

entry.title: SproutRAG: Attention-Guided Tree Search with Progressive Embeddings for Long-Document RAG

author.name: Amirhossein Abaskohi, Issam H. Laradji, Peter West, Giuseppe Carenini

entry.summary: SproutRAG is an attention-guided hierarchical RAG framework that organizes sentence-level chunks into progressively larger semantically coherent units using learned inter-sentence attention to build a binary chunking tree. It balances retrieval granularity and contextual coherence without costly LLM calls during indexing.

entry.title: Possible or Definite? A Benchmark for Evaluating Diagnostic Uncertainty Preservation in Clinical Text

author.name: Hongbo Du, Zixin Lu, Jiaming Qu

entry.summary: This work constructs a benchmark of 1,200 clinical documents with over 9,000 uncertainty annotations across five levels to evaluate whether LLMs preserve diagnostic uncertainty (e.g., possible vs definite pneumonia) when summarizing or revising clinical text. Altering uncertainty expressions can change clinical meaning entirely.

entry.title: Lost in a Single Vector: Improving Long-Document Retrieval with Chunk Evidence Aggregation

author.name: Shanshan Lyu, Yiwei Wang, Yujun Cai, Jiafeng Guo, Shenghua Liu

entry.summary: DICE is a training-free document-side strategy for long-document dense retrieval that splits documents into chunks, encodes them independently with a frozen model, and aggregates back into a single vector to preserve decisive short spans. It introduces the Evidence Dilution Index to measure how document-level representations underrepresent strong chunk evidence.

entry.title: SenFlow: Inter-Sentence Flow Modeling for AI-Generated Text Detection in Hybrid Documents

author.name: Jingkun Luo, Yifan Sun, Da-Tian Peng, Guanxiong Pei

entry.summary: SenFlow recasts sentence-level AI-generated text detection in hybrid human-LLM documents as structured prediction over sentence sequences, combining graph-based inter-sentence propagation with CRF decoding. It introduces MOSAIC, a 16,000-document benchmark generated by recent models like DeepSeek-V3.2 and Kimi K2 with perplexity-consistency filtering.

entry.title: RECOM: A Validity Discrimination Tradeoff in Automatic Metrics for Open Ended Reddit Question Answering

author.name: Pushwitha Krishnappa, Amit Das, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha, Tathagata Mukherjee

entry.summary: Introduces RECOM, a contamination-free dataset of 15,000 r/AskReddit questions with authentic community replies postdating model cutoffs, to study a tension in automatic metrics between validity and discriminative power. Finds no metric does both jobs well for open-ended QA.

entry.title: Intrinsic 4D Gaussian Segmentation from Scene Cues

author.name: Hasan Yazar, Mohamed Rayan Barhdadi, Erchin Serpedin, Mehmet Tuncel, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: Investigates recovering object-level segmentation directly from dynamic 4D Gaussian Splatting scene cues rather than importing and distilling 2D foundation-model masks across frames. Aims to reduce cost and dependence on external mask quality for 4D segmentation.

entry.title: PorTEXTO: A European Portuguese Benchmark for Visual Text Extraction

author.name: Jo\~ao Cardeira, Diogo Gl\'oria-Silva, Manuel Letras da Luz, Rafael Ferreira, Diogo Tavares, David Semedo, Jo\~ao Magalh\~aes

entry.summary: PorTEXTO is the first benchmark for contemporary European Portuguese visual text extraction (OCR), built with frontier-LVLM transcriptions reviewed by native speakers. It documents a sharp performance drop on real-world samples and shows specialized multilingual data outperforms model scale.

entry.title: ProductConsistency: Improving Product Identity Preservation in Instruction-Based Image Editing via SFT and RL

author.name: Mukund Khanna, Raj Singh Yadav, Kunal Singh

entry.summary: Introduces the ProductConsistency dataset and an SFT-plus-RL pipeline to preserve product identity, branding, and text fidelity during instruction-based image editing. It targets a commercially relevant gap where editing models distort product features.

entry.title: CABLE: Cloud-Assisted Bandwidth-efficient LMM-based Encoding for V2X Systems

author.name: Haohua Que, Zhipeng Bao, Qianyi Wu, Handong Yao

entry.summary: CABLE is a bandwidth-efficient edge-cloud framework that uploads only region-of-interest masked images for cloud-hosted large multimodal model perception in vehicle-to-everything systems. It propagates prior segmentation masks with ego-motion compensation to cut communication and latency.

entry.title: SRL: Combining SLIP Model and Reinforcement Learning for Agile Robotic Jumping

author.name: Xiaowen Hu, Linqi Ye, Yudi Zhu, Chenyue Shao, Rankun Li, Qingdu Li, Yan Peng

entry.summary: SRL combines the physically grounded Spring-Loaded Inverted Pendulum model with reinforcement learning for agile robotic jumping, using SLIP as a guided baseline to accelerate RL adaptation on irregular terrain. It aims to merge SLIP's biological plausibility with RL's environmental adaptability.

entry.title: ZiMPedance: Impedance-Aware ZMP Modeling and Control for Payload Carrying with Quadruped Robots

author.name: Giovanni B. Dessy, Lorenzo Amatucci, Victor Barasuol, Claudio Semini

entry.summary: ZiMPedance derives an extended Zero Moment Point formulation incorporating passive spring-damper payload-interface dynamics for quadruped payload transport, integrating it into model predictive control. It shows underdamped configurations can resonate with locomotion harmonics and degrade stability.

entry.title: C-ARC: Continuous-Adaptive Range Clustering for Non-Repetitive LiDAR Sensors

author.name: Nick B. Schroeder (Technical University of Darmstadt, Darmstadt, Germany), Jonathan Lichtenfeld (Simulation, Systems Optimization and Robotics Group, Technical University of Darmstadt, Darmstadt, Germany), Oskar von Stryk (Simulation, Systems Optimization and Robotics Group, Technical University of Darmstadt, Darmstadt, Germany)

entry.summary: C-ARC is a continuous-adaptive range clustering method designed for non-repetitive Risley prism LiDAR sensors, which violate assumptions of structured scan lines and frame boundaries used by conventional clustering. It enables real-time clustering on increasingly popular low-cost non-repetitive sensors.

entry.title: ReSiReg: Towards Spatially Consistent Semantics in Language-Conditioned Robotic Tasks

author.name: Simon Schwaiger, David Seyser, Alessandro Scherl, Wilfried W\"ober, Gerald Steinbauer-Wagner

entry.summary: ReSiReg improves dense language-grounded retrieval by reconstructing patch features as soft mixtures of prototype-level language embeddings, addressing noisy and spatially inconsistent VLM embeddings. It targets robotic tasks needing joint semantic and 3D-spatial reasoning.

entry.title: ART-VS: Adaptive Resolution Tiling for Vision Transformer Visual Servoing

author.name: Alessandro Scherl, Bernhard Neuberger, Simon Schwaiger, David Mulero-P\'erez, Lucas Muster, Jose Garcia-Rodriguez

entry.summary: ART-VS is a two-phase adaptive resolution tiling method for self-supervised Vision Transformer visual servoing that uses coarse patches for stable alignment then tiled high-resolution features for precision. It addresses the robustness-precision trade-off where simply increasing resolution yields marginal robustness gains.

entry.title: MapSatisfyBench: Benchmarking Satisfaction-Aware Map Agents through Behavior-Grounded Implicit Decision Factors

author.name: Lubin Bai, Mengyu Cao, Sixue Wang, Zhongwei Wan, Yue Pan, Jiale Hou, Xiang Li, Xiuyuan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces MapSatisfyBench, a benchmark evaluating map agents on recovering implicit decision factors from underspecified everyday queries. It grounds evaluation in user behavior to assess proactive satisfaction-aware reasoning.

entry.title: FllumaOne: A Code-Native Multimodal CAD Dataset with Executable Programs and Kernel-Validated Feature Histories

author.name: Jizong Zhan

entry.summary: Introduces FllumaOne, a code-native multimodal CAD dataset of 100K models generated by executable Python programs with feature trees, STEP geometry, point clouds, and renderings. It supports editable CAD research by exposing modeling operations and dependencies.

entry.title: Prefill/Decode-Aware Evaluation of LLM Inference on Emerging AI Accelerators

author.name: Shun Usami, Venkatram Vishwanath, E. Wes Bethel

entry.summary: This paper presents a phase-aware (Prefill/Decode) evaluation of LLM inference across GPUs and emerging AI accelerators using Llama2-7B, capturing distinct latency characteristics via TTFT and TPOT. It clarifies when alternative accelerators outperform GPUs for inference.

entry.title: MeiBRD: Meta-Learning Intraoperative Biomechanical Residual Deformation

author.name: Casey Meisenzahl, Jon Heiselman, Michael Holtz, Yubo Ye, Michael Miga, Linwei Wang
