entry.title: Capability Minimization as a Safety Primitive: Risk-Aware Causal Gating for Least-Privilege LLM Agents

author.name: Laxmipriya Ganesh Iyer and Rahul Suresh Babu

entry.summary: Introduces Risk-Aware Causal Gating (RACG), a framework deciding whether an LLM agent should act, defer, or abstain based on counterfactual risk estimation with distribution-free bounds. Frames capability minimization as a safety primitive for least-privilege agents.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Visual Questioner

author.name: Yijun Liang, Hengguang Zhou, Ming Li, Lichen Li, Cho-Jui Hsieh, Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes a self-evolving framework where a vision-language model acts as both proposer and filter to generate increasingly hard, informative, visual-centric questions to train itself without external supervision. Improves the underexplored active-questioning ability of VLMs.

entry.title: Dialogue SWE-Bench: A Benchmark for Dialogue-Driven Coding Agents

author.name: Brendan King and Jeffrey Flanigan

entry.summary: Presents Dialogue SWE-Bench, a benchmark evaluating coding agents in interactive dialogue-driven settings rather than as fully autonomous systems, using a persona-grounded user simulator. A proposed schema-guided agent improves dialogue capabilities by 3-14 percent over baselines.

entry.title: Utility-Constrained Policy Optimization

author.name: Mehrdad Moghimi, Bernardo Avila Pires

entry.summary: Introduces a practical methodology for utility-constrained MDPs that supports risk-sensitive constraints, overcoming a limitation of standard constrained MDPs that allow mixing catastrophic and overly conservative behaviors. It provides the first practical solution for UCMDPs in constrained RL.

entry.title: WAM4D: Fast 4D World Action Model via Spatial Register Tokens

author.name: Ying Li, Xiaobao Wei, Jiajun Cao, Hao Wang, Xiaowei Chi, Chengyu Bai, Qianpu Sun, Jiajun Li, Xiaojie Zhang, Jian Tang, Sirui Han, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: WAM4D is a fast 4D world action model for robotic manipulation that uses lightweight spatial register tokens as training-time future-depth readouts to inject 3D geometric priors without slowing causal action generation. It bridges the gap between 2D video world models and the 3D spatial constraints needed for precise manipulation.

entry.title: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enough: A Failure-Mode Study of GUI Agents

author.name: Seoyoung Choi, Minseok Ko, Hyunseok Lee, Kunwoong Kim, Woomin Song, Chanseok Jeon, and Jinwoo Shin

entry.summary: Conducts a failure-mode study of visual memory in GUI agents, introducing a taxonomy of four failure types to analyze which failures visual memory mitigates versus exacerbates. Finds naive visual memory is insufficient, challenging the assumption that storing past screenshots reliably improves agent decisions.

entry.title: Closing the Reflection Gap: A Free Calibration Bonus for Agentic RL

author.name: Yinglun Zhu

entry.summary: This work identifies a reflection gap where LLM agents mis-assess their own outputs even after environment feedback, and proposes RefGRPO, which adds a calibration bonus contrasting self-reflection with actual outcomes. It requires no extra reward model or judge.

entry.title: Operator Calculus for Population-Based Optimization: A Mean-Field Convergence Theory

author.name: Pekka Malo, Lauri Viitasaari, Patrik Nummi, Antti Suominen, Ankur Sinha, and Olli Tahvonen

entry.summary: This paper introduces an operator calculus that describes a broad class of population-based optimization methods as compositions of mutation, selection, and recombination operators on probability measures. It establishes a mean-field convergence theory unifying fragmented algorithm-specific analyses.

entry.title: A theoretical model for task routing in mixture-of-expert transformers

author.name: Yongli Xiang, Vinoth Nandakumar, Yunzhi Yao, Peike Li, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical explanation of task-expert specialization in MoE transformers using discrete language models (syntactic templates and key-value dictionaries), proving a single-layer MoE can encode knowledge through task-specialized experts. It bridges a gap between empirical MoE observations and theory.

entry.title: A Fixed-Point Neural Operator for Size- and Functional-Transferable Hamiltonian Prediction

author.name: Yunhong Lou, Xihang Yue, Xinran Wei, Tianqi Deng, Linchao Zhu

entry.summary: HamEvo is a neural operator that learns the single-step self-consistent field update and returns the converged Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian as its fixed point, transferable across molecule sizes and functionals. It improves ML-accelerated DFT by respecting the SCF fixed-point structure.

entry.title: Behavioral Audit of Machine Unlearning Has a Privacy Cost

author.name: Liou Tang, James Joshi, Ashish Kundu

entry.summary: This paper provides an information-theoretic proof that, for convex models, behavioral auditing of machine unlearning under mutual distrust cannot identify insufficiently unlearned models without leaking membership information. It establishes a fundamental privacy cost of MU auditing.

entry.title: $\mu_0$: A Scalable 3D Interaction-Trace World Model

author.name: Seungjae Lee, Yoonkyo Jung, Jusuk Lee, Jonghun Shin, Amir Hossein Shahidzadeh, Yao-Chih Lee, H. Jin Kim, Jia-Bin Huang, Furong Huang

entry.summary: Mu0 is a scalable 3D interaction-trace world model that forecasts smooth 3D trajectories for salient points (objects, tools, hands, contact regions) instead of dense pixels or embodiment-specific actions, with an automatic TraceExtract supervision system. It provides a compact, embodiment-agnostic motion interface for robot learning.

entry.title: Recursively Trained Diffusion Models: Limiting Collapse Distribution and Spectral Characterization

author.name: Na\"il B. Khelifa, Richard E. Turner, Ramji Venkataramanan

entry.summary: This paper proves that recursively trained diffusion models converge geometrically to a unique limiting distribution characterized as an infinite Gaussian-smoothed mixture, isolating early-stopping of reverse diffusion as a collapse mechanism distinct from imperfect learning. It answers what distribution recursion converges to and how fast.

entry.title: Avatar V: Scaling Video-Reference Avatar Video Generation

author.name: Benjamin Liang, Ce Chen, Desmond Lin, Ivan Somov, Jiajun Zhao, Jiewei Yuan, Jingfeng Zhang, Junhao Huang, Nik Nolte, Pedram Haqiqi, Penghan Wang, Rong Yan, Rui Zhang, Sam Prokopchuk, Sivan Wang, Viktor Goriachko, Yi Ren, Yuanming Li, Yutao Chen, Zhenhui Ye, Zhibin Hong, Zilong Nie, Zujin Guo

entry.summary: Avatar V is a production-scale framework for generating behaviorally faithful avatar videos by conditioning on the full token sequence of a reference video rather than a single static image. It captures talking rhythm, gestures, and expression dynamics.

entry.title: ContactWorld: What Matters in Vision-Tactile World Models for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhang, Pokuang Zhou, Kaidi Zhang, Adeesh Desai, Temitope Amosa, Davood Soleymanzadeh, Jiuzhou Lei, Minghui Zheng, Yu She

entry.summary: ContactWorld is a benchmark and empirical study of vision-tactile world models across 12 contact-rich manipulation tasks, finding that spatially structured and temporally continuous representations (e.g., point clouds) yield the best planning performance. It clarifies what representation properties matter.

entry.title: Minim: Privacy-Aware Minimal View for Agents via Trusted Local Sanitization

author.name: Hexuan Yu, Chaoyu Zhang, Heng Jin, Shanghao Shi, Ning Zhang, Y. Thomas Hou, Wenjing Lou

entry.summary: MINIM is a trusted local broker that minimizes UI state observations before they leave a device for LLM agents, learning per-element sensitivity and task-necessity scores grounded in Contextual Integrity. It prevents leaking sensitive context like authentication codes to remote servers.

entry.title: Formalizing Numerical Analysis: An Agent Pipeline and Quality Audit Beyond Kernel Acceptance

author.name: Theodore Meek, Siyuan Ge, Di Qiu Xiang, Simon Chess, Vasily Ilin

entry.summary: Applies a coding agent to formalize a numerical analysis textbook in Lean 4 covering territory largely absent from mathlib, and introduces a three-dimensional quality framework (semantic correctness, mathlib reuse, cross-file reuse) that goes beyond mere kernel acceptance. It stresses agent capacity to develop new theory rather than reuse existing libraries.

entry.title: Encoder Winners Do Not Reliably Transfer Across VLA Backbone Scale: A Frozen-Backbone Grafting Diagnostic

author.name: Qingping Zeng, Fei She

entry.summary: Introduces a frozen-backbone grafting diagnostic that swaps a VLA's vision encoder under a fixed protocol to test whether encoder choices validated on small VLAs transfer to larger backbones. Across four encoders, two LIBERO suites, and two backbones (SmolVLA-450M, pi-0.5-3.3B), finds small-backbone encoder winners do not reliably transfer to larger ones.

entry.title: Universal Manipulation Exoskeleton: Learning Compliant Whole-body Policies with Real-time Torque Feedback

author.name: Litian Liang, Jingxi Xu, Xinda Qi, Yujun Cai, Houzhu Ding, Luqi Wang, Zhixin Sun, Jyh-Herng Chow, Ming Yang, Mark Cutkosky

entry.summary: UME is a low-cost upper-limb exoskeleton that provides real-time haptic torque feedback while recording whole-arm configurations and joint torques for teleoperation. It enables learning compliant whole-body manipulation policies including blindfolded constrained tasks.

entry.title: HarnessX: A Composable, Adaptive, and Evolvable Agent Harness Foundry

author.name: Tingyang Chen, Shuo Lu, Kang Zhao, Weicheng Meng, Hanlin Teng, Tianhao Li, Chao Li, Xule Liu, Jian Liang, Zhizhong Zhang, Yuan Xie, Heng Qu, Kun Shao, Jian Luan

entry.summary: HarnessX is a foundry for composable, adaptive, and evolvable agent harnesses, assembling typed primitives via a substitution algebra and evolving them through a trace-driven multi-agent engine grounded in a symbolic-RL mirror. It closes the harness-model loop by turning trajectories into harness updates.

entry.title: Machine-learned particle flow as a foundation model for collider physics

author.name: Farouk Mokhtar, Joosep Pata, Michael Kagan, Javier Duarte

entry.summary: This work repurposes a machine-learned particle-flow reconstruction model as a foundation model for collider physics, appending its per-particle latent representations as features for jet flavor identification, jet energy regression, and missing momentum regression. It demonstrates a shared representation linking low-level detector data to high-level analysis tasks.

entry.title: Beyond the Training Distribution: Evaluating Predictions Under Distribution Shift and Selection Bias

author.name: Annie Ulichney and Amanda Coston

entry.summary: This work presents a double machine learning procedure for pre-deployment model evaluation under joint covariate shift and selective labeling (outcomes observed based on historical decisions). It provides identification results and bias analysis for estimating target risk of black-box models.

entry.title: SIMMER: Benchmarking Latent Failures in LLM Executable Planning with a World Model

author.name: Xiaoxin Lu, Ranran Haoran Zhang, Rui Zhang

entry.summary: SIMMER is a benchmark for evaluating latent failures in LLM executable planning, where plans execute but silently compromise goals, using a human-curated symbolic kitchen world model with 77 actions and 262 objects. It targets a critical, under-evaluated failure mode beyond simple execution success.

entry.title: Deep Learning Based Superconductivity: Prediction and Experimental Tests

author.name: Daniel Kaplan, Adam Zhang, Joanna Blawat, Rongying Jin, Robert J. Cava, Viktor Oudovenko, Gabriel Kotliar, Anirvan M. Sengupta and Weiwei Xie

entry.summary: Researchers built a deep learning model that predicts new superconducting materials using only chemical composition as input, then experimentally synthesized and confirmed a predicted compound. The approach is contrasted with random forest methods that require richer chemical features.

entry.title: The Weight Norm Sets the Grokking Timescale: A Causal Delay Law

author.name: Truong Xuan Khanh, Doan Hoang Viet, Luu Duc Trung, Phan Thanh Duc

entry.summary: This paper intervenes on weight norm during training to show it causally sets the grokking timescale: free training groks at a near-invariant critical norm, and clamping the norm yields an exponential delay law. It establishes a quantitative causal delay law with a near-universal exponent.

entry.title: SEVRA-BENCH: Social Engineering of Vulnerabilities in Review Agents

author.name: Rui Melo, Riccardo Fogliato, Sean Zhou, Pratiksha Thaker, Zhiwei Steven Wu

entry.summary: SEVRA-BENCH measures how often LLM code reviewers approve adversarial pull requests where the attacker controls both code and PR text, built by inverting real CVE-fixing commits. It probes whether automated reviewers can resist social engineering in PR workflows.

entry.title: Poker Arena: Multi-Axis Profiling of Strategic Reasoning and Memory in LLMs

author.name: Pratham Singla, Shivank Garg, Vihan Singh

entry.summary: Presents Poker Arena, a no-limit Texas Hold'em benchmark with a three-layer memory architecture and nine-axis cognitive profiling to decompose strategic reasoning in frontier LLMs. It shows tournament outcomes and aggregate skill scores rank models differently.

entry.title: Closed-loop discovery of out-of-distribution processing protocols by evolutionary search and uncertainty-aware learning

author.name: Yu Liu, Stanislav Udovenko, Ching-Che Lin, Jaegyu Kim, Lane W. Martin, Susan Trolier-McKinstry and Sergei V. Kalinin

entry.summary: Introduces a closed-loop materials discovery workflow coupling evolutionary search over processing waveforms with uncertainty-aware deep kernel learning to find out-of-distribution protocols. Applied to ferroelectric thin films with experimental validation.

entry.title: PhysVLA: Towards Physically-Grounded VLA for Embodied Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Namai Chandra, Shriram Damodaran, Lin Wang

entry.summary: PhysVLA is a plug-and-play inference-time framework that wraps any frozen vision-language-action model to enforce physical principles like rigid-body dynamics and contact constraints with under 1ms overhead. It addresses the physics gap left by behavior-cloned VLAs.

entry.title: Harsher on Male? Evaluating LLMs on Gender-Asymmetric Moral Framing Across Diverse Conflict Scenarios

author.name: Guangzong Si, Dong Wang, Zhenhao Li, Yifan Yu, Panwang Pan, Wentao Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces GAMA-Bench, a gender-mirrored benchmark of 1,298 matched conflict scenarios to test whether LLMs apply consistent response standards to identical misconduct by male versus female actors. Measures allocation of punishment, empathy, escalation, and blame across 10 models.

entry.title: Rethinking Backdoor Adversarial Unlearning through the Lens of Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Learning

author.name: Zhenqian Zhu, Yamin Hu, Yujiang Liu, Luping Wei, Wenbo Hou, Bin Li, Haodong Li, Wenjian Luo

entry.summary: Reformulates backdoor learning and unlearning as a three-stage continual learning process and derives necessary conditions for complete backdoor unlearning based on catastrophic forgetting. Proposes BI-BAU (Blind Inversion-Backdoor Adversarial Unlearning) to fully eliminate backdoor effects.

entry.title: Numbers Already Carry Their Own Embeddings

author.name: Suhyun Bae, Donghun Lee

entry.summary: Introduces Adelic operation-preserved embeddings, a training-free representation capturing both a number's real value and its p-adic modular signatures, preserving additive and multiplicative structure. It is plug-and-play, drops into existing architectures, and achieves the first perfect accuracy on the Weaving Pattern algebraic combinatorics task.

entry.title: VideoWeave: Unlocking Geometric Consistency in Video Generation via Joint Geometry-Video Modeling

author.name: Xunzhi Xiang, Zixuan Duan, Yabo Chen, Zhengxuan Wei, Guiyu Zhang, Zixiao Gu, Zhe Gao, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Qi Fan, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: VideoWeave is a latent-space post-training framework that improves 3D geometric consistency in video generation by constraining the generative distribution with implicit geometry-model features rather than explicit depth or point cloud reconstructions. This avoids sensitivity to errors from upstream geometry pipelines.

entry.title: Robustness without Wrinkles: Parallel Simulation and Robust MPC for Certified Deformable Manipulation

author.name: Wei-Chen Li, Jeffrey Fang, Sasanka Polisetti, Yuexi Song, Glen Chou

entry.summary: CORD-SLS combines a GPU-parallel differentiable simulator with robust output-feedback MPC and conformal prediction to enable certified safe manipulation of deformable objects like ropes and cloth. The integration of contact smoothing, robust control, and calibrated perception bounds is a solid robotics contribution.

entry.title: SkillAudit: Ground-Truth-Free Skill Evolution via Paired Trajectory Auditing

author.name: Haowen Gao, Haoran Chen, Can Wang, Shasha Guo, Liang Pang, Zhaoyang Liu, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: SkillAudit evolves agent skills without ground-truth feedback via paired trajectory auditing, running the same task with and without a candidate skill to isolate behavioral changes. This enables skill refinement when only task descriptions and workspace data are available.

entry.title: Decoupled Mixture-of-Experts for Parametric Knowledge Injection

author.name: Baoqing Yue, Weihang Su, Qingyao Ai, Yichen Tang, Changyue Wang, Jiacheng Kang, Jingtao Zhan, Yiqun Liu

entry.summary: DMoE is a modular Mixture-of-Experts architecture for parametric knowledge injection that decouples experts and the router from the base model, converting external corpora into independently updatable expert modules. An uncertainty-aware router selects experts to mitigate forgetting and conflict.

entry.title: FloVerse: Floor Plan-Guided Multi-Modal Navigation

author.name: Weiqi Huang, Shuangyi Dong, Jiaxin Li, Yifei Guo, Zan Wang, Wei Liang

entry.summary: FloVerse introduces a floor-plan-guided embodied navigation task unifying PointNav, ObjectNav, and ImageNav, with a 1.6K-scene dataset of 240K trajectories and 12M RGBD frames. ThreeDiff, a two-stage diffusion-based imitation policy, serves as the method.

entry.title: Causal Object-Centric Models for Planning with Monte Carlo Tree Search

author.name: Rodion Vakhitov, Leonid Ugadiarov, Alexey Skrynnik, Aleksandr Panov

entry.summary: COMET performs Monte Carlo Tree Search in a slot-structured object-centric latent space, combining a frozen object encoder with a transformer world model and object-causal attention for focused decision-making. It adds explicit object-level inductive bias to MuZero-style planning across diverse RL tasks.

entry.title: PepALD: Macrocyclic Peptide Generation via Autoregressive Latent Diffusion

author.name: Junming Zhang, Siyu Yi, Wei Ju, Zhonghui Gu

entry.summary: PepALD is an autoregressive latent diffusion foundation model for de novo macrocyclic peptide generation that uses structured chemical embeddings, R-group-aware ring closures, and affinity-aligned denoising. It targets simultaneous control of non-natural chemistry, ring topology, permeability, and binding.

entry.title: StreamMemBench: Streaming Evaluation of Agent Memory for Future-Oriented Assistance

author.name: Guanming Liu, Yuqi Ren, Hansu Gu, Peng Zhang, Weihang Wang, Jiahao Liu, Ning Gu, and Tun Lu

entry.summary: StreamMemBench is a streaming benchmark for personal-agent memory that constructs two-step task sequences around evidence anchors from egocentric streams, testing both evidence use and reuse of feedback for future assistance. It evaluates the trajectory from streaming observations to later future-oriented assistance, which prior benchmarks miss.

entry.title: How Task Structure Limits Multi-Agent Success: An Information-Theoretic Analysis

author.name: Shi Pan, Ming Luo

entry.summary: This information-theoretic analysis proves that multi-agent system success probability decays exponentially with an information bottleneck determined by the minimum-cut cost of the task's constraint graph, given bounded inter-agent communication. It bounds when collaboration cannot overcome single-agent limits.

entry.title: When Plausible Is Not Realistic: Evaluating Human Mobility in LLM-Based Urban Simulation

author.name: Gustavo H. Santos, Aline Carneiro Viana, Thiago H. Silva

entry.summary: Introduces a validation framework testing whether LLM-based urban simulation agents reproduce empirically realistic human mobility rather than just plausible narratives. Finds a substantial gap between narrative plausibility and real mobility data in Paris and Shanghai.

entry.title: AnyGoal: Vision-Language Guided Multi-Agent Exploration for Training-Free Lifelong Navigation

author.name: MoniJesu James, Marcelino Julio Fernando, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: AnyGoal is a training-free multi-robot navigation architecture placing a VLM at the core of frontier-based exploration, coordinating agents via a shared 2D Gaussian Bayesian value map. It supports lifelong navigation without resets and generalizes across goal modalities.

entry.title: HiLo-Token: Input-Adaptive High-Low Frequency Token Compression for Efficient Image Editing

author.name: Haoran You, Yotam Nitzan, Lingzhi Zhang, Yifan Gong, Mang-Tik Chiu, Connelly Barnes, Yan Kang, Yuqian Zhou, Eli Shechtman, Sohrab Amirghodsi

entry.summary: HiLo-Token is an input-adaptive token compression framework for diffusion transformers in image editing, allocating more token budget to high-frequency regions to reduce latency. Targets the DiT bottleneck that dominates editing latency in tools like Photoshop.

entry.title: Smoothing Dark Areas in Molecular Latent Diffusion

author.name: Xi Wang, Jiahan Li, Yuxuan Xia, Yingcheng Wu, Shaoyi Zheng, Shengjie Wang

entry.summary: Identifies dark areas in molecular latent diffusion: latent regions reachable during sampling that decode to invalid molecules, and proposes TopVAE, a topology-optimized VAE that internalizes structural and chemical constraints in the decoder. Addresses the strict validity requirements of molecular generation.

entry.title: Self-Improving VLA Policies: Selected Diffusion Noise for Spurious-Robust Action Smoothing

author.name: Duc Minh Nguyen, Bao-Ngoc Dao, Tung M. Luu, Binh Gia Nguyen, Vinh Tong, Anji Liu, Vu N. Duong, Dung D. Le, Daniel Sonntag, Trung Le, Ngan Le, Jan Peter, An Thai Le, Minh Nhat Vu, Mathias Niepert, Khoa D. Doan, Duy M. H. Nguyen, Vien Anh Ngo

entry.summary: Introduces Selected Diffusion Noise, a training-free test-time method for diffusion-based VLA policies that samples noise vectors maximally separated from a reference set to reduce reliance on spurious visual cues and improve action trajectory coherence. It improves robustness and success rate without modifying parameters.

entry.title: Robin-Neumann Coupling of PINN and FEM Solvers: A Steklov-Poincar\'e View, with Application to Fluid-Structure Interaction with Contact

author.name: Mikel Landajuela

entry.summary: Puts PINN-FEM coupling on a domain-decomposition footing by viewing each solver as a Steklov-Poincare operator, transferring Dirichlet-Neumann diagnosis and a Robin-Neumann cure with closed-form interface impedance. Proves a PINN-specific contraction theorem accounting for training residuals, applied to fluid-structure interaction with contact.

entry.title: When and How Severely: Scenario-Specific Safety Envelopes for Driving VLAs

author.name: Abhinaw Priyadershi and Jelena Frtunikj

entry.summary: This work evaluates scenario-specific safety envelopes for a 10B driving Vision-Language-Action planner under ISO 21448, finding that aggregate safe thresholds mask scenarios tolerating higher perturbations. A GMM identifies discrete severity bands beyond mean-error measures.

entry.title: CausalMotion: Structured Physical Reasoning as Keyframe and Trajectory Guidance for Training-Free Video Generation

author.name: Sihan Zhuang, Xinyuan Chen, Tianfan Xue, Yaohui Wang

entry.summary: CausalMotion is a training-free framework injecting explicit physical reasoning into video generation by using a vision-language model to produce keyframe and trajectory guidance for diffusion models. It targets physically consistent, causally plausible long-horizon dynamics.

entry.title: Scratched Lenses, Shifted Depth: Passive Camera-Side Optical Attacks

author.name: Qinlin He, Zeming Zhuang, Yongji Wu, Lan Zhang, and Xiaoyong (Brian) Yuan

entry.summary: This paper introduces SLASH, a passive camera-side optical attack where small scratches on a lens produce trigger-conditioned optical artifacts that bias geometric inference (e.g., depth) under specific visual conditions. It reveals a persistent physical threat distinct from scene-based adversarial attacks.

entry.title: Regional Climate Model Emulation with Diffusion Approaches: What is the Added Value of Generative Machine Learning?

author.name: Mikel N. Legasa, Antoine Doury, Achille Gellens, Redouane Lguensat, Clara Naldesi, Soulivanh Thao, Mathieu Vrac

entry.summary: This paper introduces ParamDiffusion, a two-stage diffusion framework for emulating regional climate models, and critically assesses whether generative ML provides added value via the ensemble uncertainty envelope for precipitation downscaling. It evaluates generative emulators against state-of-the-art baselines.

entry.title: GAGPO: Generalized Advantage Grouped Policy Optimization

author.name: Siyuan Zhu, Chao Yu, Rongxin Yang, Zongkai Liu, Jinjun Hu, Qiwen Chen, Yibo Zhang

entry.summary: GAGPO is a critic-free RL method for multi-turn LLM agents that builds a non-parametric grouped value proxy from sampled rollouts to compute step-aligned temporal advantages, addressing sparse trajectory-level rewards. It improves credit assignment without costly value models.

entry.title: Benchmarking Web Agent Safety under E-commerce Deceptive Interfaces

author.name: Zijing Shi, Meng Fang, Ling Chen

entry.summary: WebDecept is a configurable framework that injects realistic deceptive e-commerce interface patterns (dark patterns, redirects, shopping manipulation) into web environments to test agent safety. Results show current multimodal web agents are highly susceptible to manipulation.

entry.title: A Virtuous AI is an Existential Risk

author.name: Guillermo Del Pinal and Youngchan Lee and Min Ohn

entry.summary: This paper finetunes models with a virtuous-agent, subordinate-agent, and generic-agent constitution and finds a trade-off: making AI more virtuous can increase its willingness to endorse behaviors that raise existential risk. It examines tension between Constitutional AI, virtue ethics, and safety.

entry.title: The Culture Funnel: You Can't Align What isn't in the Data

author.name: Ananya Sahu, Mehrnaz Mofakhami, Daniel D'Souza, Thomas Euyang, Julia Kreutzer, and Marzieh Fadaee

entry.summary: This paper argues that modern LLM pipelines suffer from a cultural data funnel, showing explicit cultural signals decline sharply during post-training while geographically concentrated task data dominates. It releases a culturally tagged dataset of 5.6M samples and shows tags improve cultural benchmark performance.

entry.title: FlowMo-WM: A World Model with Object Momentum and Hidden Ambient Drift

author.name: Yitao Jiang, Luyang Zhao, Muhao Chen, Devin Balkcom

entry.summary: FlowMo-WM is a visual world model for robotics that infers object momentum and hidden ambient drift (currents, wind) from image-action histories without flow supervision. It targets realistic settings like aquatic vehicles where inertia and external forces dominate.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Embodied Autonomous Driving: From V2X Information Exchange to Shared World Models

author.name: Senkang Hu, Zhengru Fang, Yihang Tao, Zihan Fang, Sam Tak Wu Kwong, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: A survey of over 380 publications on multi-agent autonomous driving through the lens of Shared World Models that maintain predictive cross-agent representations. Covers V2X communication, collaborative perception, cooperative planning, and simulation.

entry.title: SANA: What Matters for QA Agents over Massive Data Lakes?

author.name: Austin Senna Wijaya, Jiaxiang Liu, Haonan Wang, Eugene Wu

entry.summary: SANA is a diagnostic ablation framework for exploratory QA agents over data lakes that decomposes failures into search, planning, data analysis, and action policy components. It constructs idealized tools to isolate each component and diagnose policy failures.

entry.title: DLawBench: Evaluating LLMs Through Multi-Turn Legal Consultation

author.name: Li Zhang, Yuzhen Shi, Yiran Hu, Jingwen Zhang, Wenbo Lv, Yubo Ma, Wei Wang, Rongyao Shi, Yuanyang Qiu, Xinran Xu, Yuemeng Qi, Linlin Miao, Jaromir Savelka, Yun Liu, Kevin Ashley, Bing Zhao, Hu Wei, and Lin Qu

entry.summary: DLawBench is a diagnostic benchmark for multi-turn legal consultation that evaluates LLMs on eliciting material facts and guiding clients across four interaction types (cooperative, dependent, withdrawn, adversarial). It fills a gap in interactive legal-reasoning evaluation.

entry.title: Can Post-Training Turn LLMs into Good Medical Coders? An Empirical Study of Generative ICD Coding

author.name: Ziqing Wang, Weihao Li, Shijie Chen, Yuan Luo, Kaize Ding

entry.summary: An empirical study of post-training (supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning) for generative LLM-based ICD medical coding under a common protocol, challenging the view that LLMs are weak coders. The first to evaluate RL-based post-training for generative ICD coding.

entry.title: MedLatentDx: Latent Multi-Agent Communication for Cross-Hospital Rare-Disease Diagnosis

author.name: Ziqing Wang, Lili Zhao, Kaize Ding

entry.summary: MedLatentDx is a latent multi-agent communication framework for privacy-preserving cross-hospital rare-disease diagnosis, where hospital agents keep clinical records local and exchange latent rather than textual evidence. Addresses privacy regulations limiting clinical text sharing.

entry.title: Prompt2Effect: Training-Free Image-to-Video Model Specialization via LoRA Generation

author.name: Xiaomeng Yang, Yanyu Li, Gordon Guocheng Qian, Ivan Skorokhodov, Viacheslav Ivanov, Avalon Vinella, Xuan Zhang, Yanzhi Wang, Sergey Tulyakov, and Anil Kag

entry.summary: Prompt2Effect is a hypernetwork that synthesizes effect-specific LoRA weights for image-to-video models in a single forward pass, conditioned on the frozen base model weights rather than just semantics. It amortizes per-effect LoRA training for interactive video effect control.

entry.title: Adaptive Nucleus Truncation for Long-Form Reasoning

author.name: Ousmane Amadou Dia

entry.summary: Introduces Adaptive Nucleus Truncation Sampling (ANTS), extending top-n-sigma sampling from a fixed rule into an adaptive rollout-control mechanism for long-form reasoning that adapts truncation based on entropy and task difficulty. Addresses the limitations of fixed thresholds in long decoding.

entry.title: RT-VLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Models via Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Xiangyu Huang, Zhenlin Hua, Han Zhou, Shounak Sural, Ragunathan Rajkumar

entry.summary: RT-VLA distills a state-of-the-art vision-language-action driving model into a compact student via multi-level supervised distillation, preserving language-based reasoning and post-hoc explainability while removing inference latency for real-time autonomous driving. It addresses the deployment bottleneck of large VLA backbones.

entry.title: From Attacks to Curricula: Learnability-Guided Adversarial Training for Safe Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yuewen Mei, Tong Nie, Jie Sun, Haotian Shi, Wei Ma, Jian Sun

entry.summary: Proposes AlignADV, a learnability-guided closed-loop adversarial training framework for autonomous driving that converts adversarial scenarios into resolvable, capability-aligned curricula. It reformulates scenario generation as preference alignment to avoid unsolvable extreme situations that degrade learning.

entry.title: ReactSim-Bench: Benchmarking Reactive Behavior World Model Simulation in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhang, Yanlun Peng, Jianing Zhang, Xianda Guo, Zehan Huang, Haoran Liu, Qifeng Li, Shaofeng Zhang, Xiaosong Jia, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: ReactSim-Bench is a benchmark for evaluating the reactive capability of behavior world model simulators in autonomous driving, decoupling AV control from surrounding agent control so agents respond to off-log AV behaviors as independent inputs. It addresses the lack of direct reactive capability measurement in existing benchmarks.

entry.title: FAConformer: Frequency-Aware Convolutional Transformer for Auditory Attention Decoding

author.name: Ziwei Wang, Xingyi He, Tianwang Jia, Hongbin Wang, and Dongrui Wu

entry.summary: Examines whether LLMs recommend recently banned or withdrawn pharmaceuticals in clinical questions and tests a five-agent Trust but Verify system with post-hoc adversarial auditing to reduce such errors. Uses an adversarial dataset of 103 clinical MCQs where historically correct answers now refer to banned substances, evaluating GPT-OSS, Llama-3, and Falcon-3.

entry.title: Graph-based Target Back-Propagation for Context Adaptation in Multi-LLM Agentic Systems

author.name: Tan Zhu, Tong Yao, Kananart Kuwaranancharoen, Amit Singh, Yushang Lai, Deepa Mohan, and Shankara Bhargava

entry.summary: Proposes Graph-based Target Back-Propagation (GTBP), a context adaptation framework for multi-LLM agentic workflows modeled as directed acyclic graphs that propagates local target outputs backward to guide stage-wise prompt updates. It addresses inaccurate credit assignment and provides convergence guarantees for prompt optimization without weight changes.

entry.title: Curvature-Guided Geometric Representation for Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction

author.name: Shuai Li, Chuan-Xian Ren, Yuhao Li, Ziqi Huang, Yue Pan, Mingzhe Tang and Hong Yan

entry.summary: Proposes RicciBind, a geometric representation framework for protein-ligand binding affinity prediction that uses Ricci curvature to capture local interaction tightness and optimal-transport cross-domain alignment for cross-molecular interactions. It jointly models local geometric organization and global coordinated interactions.

entry.title: From Prompts to Responses: Dual-Sided Data Leakage and Defense in Split Large Language Models

author.name: Zixuan Gu, Xiaojun Ye, Yang Liu

entry.summary: This paper reveals dual-sided privacy leakage in split LLMs, presenting PIDI, an attack that reconstructs both private input prompts and sensitive generative outputs from intermediate representations. It exposes underexplored response-side vulnerabilities in split learning deployments.

entry.title: Learning the Context of Errors: Black-Box Online Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Xilin Dai, Yiding Liu, Hongjie Xia, Yifan Hu, Zewei Dong, Jiang-Ming Yang, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: ORCA performs black-box online adaptation of time series foundation models by learning the context of predictive errors conditioned on model inputs and outputs, without needing gradient access. It targets closed-source commercial TSFM API scenarios.

entry.title: AFFORDANCE20Q: Evaluating Affordance Reasoning from Physical Properties

author.name: Yifan Jiang, Meige Yang, Zitong Li, Jay Pujara

entry.summary: Affordance20Q is a benchmark framing affordance reasoning as a 20-questions game without exposing object identity, forcing models to reason over physical properties rather than memorized mappings. It comprises over 1,000 games to probe true physical understanding in LLMs.

entry.title: HiST: A Hierarchical Sparse Transformer for Cross-Modal Spatial Transcriptomics Modeling

author.name: Weiyi Wu, Xinwen Xu, Xingjian Diao, Siting Li, Zhi Wei, Alma Andersson, Jiang Gui

entry.summary: HiST is a hierarchical sparse transformer for inferring spatial transcriptomics gene expression from H&E histology, treating measured locations as a sparse field and using sparse window attention with resolution-changing operators. It avoids dense-grid overhead and quadratic token mixing on gigapixel slides.

entry.title: Squeeze-Release: Iterative Pruning with Exact Structural Minimization

author.name: Roman Denkin, Ida Akerholm, Prashant Singh, Ida-Maria Sintorn

entry.summary: Squeeze-Release introduces an exact structural minimization that rewrites masked pruned networks into smaller dense models with identical forward functions, iterated with a release step that reactivates pruned positions as trainable noise. It includes a function-preserving CompensatedLayerNorm replacement.

entry.title: When Language Representations Interact: Separability and Cross-Lingual Effects in LLMs

author.name: Boris Marinov, Angira Sharma, Christian Schroeder de Witt, Philip Torr, Anisoara Calinescu, Jialin Yu

entry.summary: This work applies causal-geometric analysis to multilingual LLMs, studying 28 bilingual contrasts across three models to determine when languages behave as independent linear factors versus structured dependencies. It extends linear representation hypotheses to multilingual settings.

entry.title: Elastic Queries Reinforcement Learning: Self-Aware Policy Execution for VLA Models

author.name: Ge Wang, Xinyu Tan, Xiang Li, Man Luo, Chengsi Yao, Shenhao Yan, Jiahao Yang, Fan Feng, Honghao Cai, Xiangyuan Wang, Zhixin Mai, Yiming Zhao, Yatong Han, and Zhen Li

entry.summary: EQRL makes each VLA policy query elastic by jointly selecting latent input, denoising budget, and action chunk length via a lightweight adaptor trained with a difficulty-aware critic, without fine-tuning the underlying VLA. It allocates more computation to contact-rich or uncertain states.

entry.title: Hy-Embodied-0.5-VLA: From Vision-Language-Action Models to a Real-World Robot Learning Stack

author.name: He Zhang, Lingzhu Xiang, Haitao Lin, Zeyu Huang, Minghui Wang, Dingyan Zhong, Yubo Dong, Yihao Wu, Yongming Rao, Dongsheng Zhang, Wanjia He, Ling Chen, Kai Huang, Jiahao Chen, Sichang Su, Xumin Yu, Ziyi Wang, Chengwei Zhu, Xiao Teng, Yuchun Guo, Yufeng Zhang, Yuandong Liu, Rui Wang, Zisheng Lu, Han Hu, Zhengyou Zhang

entry.summary: HyVLA-0.5 is an end-to-end vision-language-action robot learning stack spanning data collection, pretraining, fine-tuning, RL post-training, and real-world deployment. It presents a full-pipeline approach to embodied robot learning.

entry.title: CADET: Physics-Grounded Causal Auditing and Training-Free Deconfounding of End-to-End Driving Planners

author.name: Zikun Guo

entry.summary: CADET is a training-free framework that audits, benchmarks, and repairs spurious causal correlations in end-to-end autonomous driving planners that associate co-occurring scene elements with driving decisions. It addresses silent causal confusion that open-loop metrics fail to detect.

entry.title: From Chatbot to Digital Colleague: The Paradigm Shift Toward Persistent Autonomous AI

author.name: Yongheng Zhang, Ziang Liu, Jiaxuan Zhu, Shuai Wang, Xiangqi Chen, Haojing Huang, Jiayi Kuang, Siyu Chen, Ao Shen, Hao Wu, Qiufeng Wang, Qian-Wen Zhang, Junnan Dong, Wenhao Jiang, Ying Shen, Hai-Tao Zheng, Yinghui Li, Di Yin, Xing Sun, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: This survey conceptualizes the transition of LLMs from chatbots to persistent autonomous digital colleagues along two axes: cognitive core (fast thinking to reasoning/reflection/RL) and tool-augmented task execution. It organizes the emerging landscape of agentic, memory-equipped, self-improving AI systems.

entry.title: Fodor and Pylyshyn's Systematicity Challenge Still Stands

author.name: Michael Goodale and Salvador Mascarenhas

entry.summary: This paper argues that Fodor and Pylyshyn's systematicity challenge for neural networks remains unsolved, contesting recent claims (e.g., Lake) that neural networks meet it. It re-examines whether neural networks explain the biconditional systematicity of human language and thought.

entry.title: TRACE: Trajectory-Routed Causal Memory for Delayed-Evidence Visuomotor Imitation

author.name: Zihao Li, Ranpeng Qiu, Yincong Chen, Guoqiang Ren, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: TRACE is a memory framework for visuomotor imitation that handles delayed-evidence tasks where an early cue disappears before a later decision, storing task-relevant evidence in bounded latent memory indexed by path signatures rather than time. It enables robots to act on no-longer-visible evidence.

entry.title: CANN-EUCLID: unsupervised constitutive artificial neural network model discovery from full-field data

author.name: Benjamin Alheit and Siddhant Kumar and Mathias Peirlinck

entry.summary: CANN-EUCLID combines constitutive artificial neural networks with the stress-unsupervised full-field EUCLID framework to discover sparse interpretable hyperelastic material laws directly from displacement fields and reaction forces in a single heterogeneous test. It enables material model discovery without homogeneous multi-loading-mode experiments, valuable for soft biological tissues.

entry.title: Zero-shot generalization of transformer neural operators to larger domains

author.name: Armand de Villeroch\'e, Sibo Cheng, Vincent Le Guen, Marc Bocquet, Rem-Sophia Mouradi, Patrick Armand, Alban Farchi, Patrick Massin

entry.summary: This work studies zero-shot generalization of transformer neural operators to spatial domains much larger than training, arguing it requires spatial locality and translation equivariance. It introduces a decomposable attention bias for controllable locality compatible with optimized attention kernels.

entry.title: Realizing Native INT8 Compute for Diffusion Transformers on Consumer GPUs: A Fused INT8 GEMM Kernel for Ideogram 4.0

author.name: Ali Asaria, Tony Salomone, Deep Gandhi

entry.summary: This paper shows that production INT8 quantization of diffusion transformers on consumer GPUs is often slower than FP8/NF4 because it dequantizes back to bf16 instead of using INT8 tensor cores, and closes the gap with a single fused Triton INT8 GEMM kernel applied to Ideogram 4.0. It realizes the actual hardware compute advantage of INT8 inference.

entry.title: Guided Diffusion with Distilled Vision-Language Reliability for Aerial Navigation

author.name: Ivan Valuev, Iana Zhura, Valerii Serpiva, Didar Seyidov and Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: Presents a reliability-aware diffusion planner for UAV navigation that conditions trajectory generation on a scene-level reliability heatmap marking untrustworthy perception regions like glass and mirrors. Distilled from a vision-language model to detect unreliable observations.

entry.title: A Two-Stage Statistical Framework for Evaluating Associative Interference in Large Language Models

author.name: Achraf Cohen and Andrew Kincaid

entry.summary: Adapts the Implicit Association Test to a controlled forced-choice framework for LLMs and introduces a two-stage model separating response compliance from task-consistent classification, addressing the conflation of refusal with task performance. Evaluates associative interference across Claude Sonnet-4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and GPT-5.

entry.title: ReactVLA: Fast and Lightweight Reactive Robot Manipulation via Improved Mean Flow Action Generation

author.name: Yanzhao Guo, Wenkai Chen, and Jianwei Zhang

entry.summary: ReactVLA is a lightweight low-latency Vision-Language-Action policy using an improved Mean Flow generator to cut diffusion sampling to one-to-few steps, plus dynamic depth-wise feature routing. It targets reactive closed-loop robot manipulation.

entry.title: Spatially Conditioned Diffusion Policy: Learning Precise and Robust Manipulation with a Single RGB Camera

author.name: Seoyoon Kim, Kanghyun Kim, Dongwoo Ko, Yeong Jin Heo, Min Jun Kim

entry.summary: Spatially Conditioned Diffusion Policy (SCDP) achieves precise robotic manipulation from a single global RGB camera by using end-effector trajectories as visual attention anchors and multi-scale feature maps. It removes the dependence on multi-camera wrist setups for fine-grained manipulation.

entry.title: A Qualitative Review of GenAI-Based Methods for Data Generation and Augmentation in Industrial Computer Vision Applications

author.name: Paul Koch, Paul Hofmann, Ferdinand Wa{\ss}elewsky, Adem Karakurt, Andre S\'ers, J\"org Kr\"uger

entry.summary: Cluster LOCO is a model-agnostic family of feature importance scores for interpreting which features drive discovered clusters, based on leave-one-covariate-out feature occlusion. It brings supervised-style feature explanations to clustering, improving auditability and reproducibility.

entry.title: PocketLLM: Ultimate Compression of Large Language Models via Meta Networks

author.name: Ye Tian, Chengcheng Wang, Jing Han, Yehui Tang, Kai Han

entry.summary: PocketLLM compresses LLM weights into a discrete latent codebook via a meta-network encoder/decoder, enabling extreme compression for edge deployment beyond what quantization or pruning achieve. The stored model is just a small decoder, codebook, and indices.

entry.title: The Coin Flip Judge? Reliability and Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation

author.name: Abel Yagubyan

entry.summary: This paper characterizes the run-to-run reliability of LLM-as-a-judge by running repeated identical evaluations, finding pairwise preferences flip ~13.6% of the time and detecting significant first-position bias. It quantifies an under-studied stochasticity in widely-used evaluation pipelines.

entry.title: When Sample Selection Bias Precipitates Model Collapse

author.name: Xinbao Qiao, Xianglong Du, Wei Liu, Jingqi Zhang, Peihua Mai, Meng Zhang, Yan Pang

entry.summary: This paper shows that under low-resource verification, where each verifier sees only a biased slice of the data manifold, data selection itself becomes biased and can precipitate model collapse during recursive training on synthetic data. It analyzes the failure in fragmented data-silo settings like healthcare and finance.

entry.title: Conformal calibration and look-elsewhere effect in anomaly detection for new-physics searches

author.name: Jack Y. Araz and Michael Spannowsky

entry.summary: This paper proposes a conformal-prediction calibration layer that turns raw anomaly-detection scores into statistically defensible significances with finite-sample guarantees, addressing look-elsewhere effects and background mismodelling in new-physics searches. It combines Mondrian/weighted conformal variants with a Gross-Vitells correction.

entry.title: Compressing Image Style Training into a Single Model Forward

author.name: Zhongjie Duan and Yingda Chen

entry.summary: Introduces i2L, a framework that predicts style LoRA weights in a single forward pass from reference images, eliminating per-style optimization for diffusion-based style transfer. This amortizes the cost of personalization while preserving stylization fidelity.

entry.title: Safety-Contract Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Network Security Response

author.name: Jose Luis Lima de Jesus Silva

entry.summary: Proposes a safety-contract graph multi-agent RL framework (ACD3-GAT) for autonomous network security response that enforces operational budgets and constraints to ensure deployability. Evaluated on the CAGE Challenge 4 cybersecurity benchmark.

entry.title: ADORE: Iterative Query Expansion with Retrieval-Grounded Relevance Feedback

author.name: Amin Bigdeli, Negar Arabzadeh, Radin Hamidi Rad, Sajad Ebrahimi, Charles L. A. Clarke, Ebrahim Bagheri

entry.summary: ADORE is an iterative query expansion framework that grounds LLM-generated expansions in actual retrieval feedback at each round, using a relevance assessor to refine the next expansion. It addresses retrieval drift from unverified single-pass generation.

entry.title: Direct/adaptive-mixture phase-gradient learning for neural-network quantum states with complex phase structure

author.name: Yi-Ran Xue, Rui Wang, Baigeng Wang, Chenan Wei

entry.summary: Identifies that optimization fragility in neural-network quantum states with complex phase structure stems from a high-variance score-function phase gradient estimator. Proposes a lower-variance direct estimator achieving low error on a 100-site flux ladder.

entry.title: SplatlessDF: Continuous Distance Field Mapping with Non-Splatting Gaussians

author.name: Monisha Mushtary Uttsha, Lan Wu and Teresa Vidal-Calleja

entry.summary: SplatlessDF is a continuous distance field mapping framework that uses anisotropic Gaussian elements from a spatial rather than photometric perspective, optimizing to recover a differentiable distance field for robot navigation. It can couple with 2D Gaussian splatting for unified surface and distance modeling.

entry.title: PostDeg: Placement Beats Parameterization in LayerNorm GNNs

author.name: Yash Tomar, Aryav Das

entry.summary: Identifies where in LayerNorm-based GNN residual blocks topology signals like degree and centrality get erased, showing the surviving slot is post-LayerNorm. It introduces PostDeg, a parameter-free inverse-degree scale yielding consistent gains, with pre-registered falsifiers.

entry.title: Non-Parametric Machine Text Detection via Multi-View Gaussian Processes

author.name: Aleem Khan, Nicholas Andrews

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-view non-parametric machine-generated text detection framework that extracts complementary feature views (stylistic, likelihood, structural) and aggregates them via a Gaussian process ensemble for robustness under paraphrasing and style-transfer attacks. It aims to avoid confidently wrong predictions under distribution shift.

entry.title: MUSE: Agentic 3D Scene Authoring via Memory-Grounded Incremental Requirement Satisfaction

author.name: Ruijie Xu, Xinnan Zhu, Jiayu Ying, Daoguo Dong, Yuzhou Ji, Xin Tan

entry.summary: MUSE is a memory-grounded multi-agent framework for text-driven 3D scene authoring formulated as incremental requirement satisfaction, unifying construction and editing with requirement-level state tracking. An Architect, Sculptor, and other agents enable part-level refinement without full-scene regeneration.

entry.title: VeriGeo: Controllable Geometry Question Generation with Numerical and Analytical Verification

author.name: Xiaoxian Duan, Zequn Liu, and Yingce Xia

entry.summary: VeriGeo is a controllable geometry question generation framework grounded in executable reasoning traces, using an Author agent to generate problems and diagrams and a Solver agent to produce proof-aligned solutions via a shared action sequence. It provides numerical and analytical verification to ensure consistency between statement, diagram, constraints, and solution.

entry.title: When Should Agent Trust Be Conditional? Characterizing and Attacking Skill-Conditional Reputation in Agent Swarms

author.name: Yihan Xia, Taotao Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies skill-conditional trust in heterogeneous LLM agent swarms, arguing global trust scores misroute tasks. It provides a phase-diagram analysis of when conditioning helps and explores attacks on skill-conditional reputation systems.

entry.title: Curvature-Informed Potential Energy Surface for Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction

author.name: Peng-Fei Sun, Chuan-Xian Ren, Hong Yan

entry.summary: CPES is a curvature-informed graph neural network for protein-ligand binding affinity that incorporates Hessian-derived curvature spectral descriptors to model conformational flexibility. It moves beyond static single-conformation geometry toward physics-informed flexibility modeling.

entry.title: One Layer's Trash is Another Layer's Treasure: Adaptive Layer-wise Visual Token Selection in LVLMs

author.name: Yongru Chen, Kai Zhang, Zeliang Zong, Yuchen Lu, Wenming Tan, Ye Ren, Jilin Hu

entry.summary: ALVTS adaptively selects different visual token subsets across layers in Large Vision-Language Models, motivated by the observation that pruned tokens may be useful in later layers. This avoids premature information loss from layer-static token pruning.

entry.title: I'm Sorry Driver, I'm Afraid I Can't Do That: Appraising the Safety of LLMs within Automotive Contexts

author.name: Shaun Feakins, Ibrahim Habli, Kim Littler, Robert Palin

entry.summary: This paper appraises the safety assurance challenges of integrating LLMs into automotive control tasks under existing standards. It highlights the dual upstream-downstream assurance burden and concrete gaps in current safety frameworks for real-time safety-critical contexts.

entry.title: Can Deep Neural Networks Improve Compression of Very Large Scientific Data?

author.name: Muhannad Alhumaidi, Guozhong Li, Spiros Skiadopoulos and Panos Kalnis

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether deep neural networks, specifically pretrained weather forecasting foundation models, can serve as superior predictors in error-bounded lossy compression of large scientific data. It leverages existing climate foundation models to avoid building compression-specific predictors.

entry.title: Be My Tutor: On-Policy Co-Distillation for Mutual LLM Improvement via Peer Feedback

author.name: Woohyeon Byeon, Jiwon Jeon, Jeonghye Kim, Youngchul Sung

entry.summary: OPCoD is an on-policy co-distillation method where two LLMs each stronger in a different domain tutor each other through peer feedback, conditioned on correct rollouts, with cognizance-based gating and feedback anchoring. It achieves mutual Pareto improvement across domains on science Q&A.

entry.title: CSPO: Constraint-Sensitive Policy Optimization for Safe Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ayoub Belouadah, Sylvain Kubler, Yves Le Traon

entry.summary: CSPO is a primal-dual safe RL method that adds a constraint-sensitive correction based on signed distance to the safety boundary, reducing oscillations and prolonged safety violations seen in standard Lagrangian methods. It improves recovery behavior in constrained MDPs.

entry.title: GitOfThoughts: Version-Controlled Reasoning and Agent Memory You Can Replay, Diff, and Merge

author.name: Pavan C Shekar, Abhishek H S, Aswanth Krishnan

entry.summary: GitOfThoughts stores an LLM agent's reasoning tree as a git repository where each scored thought is a commit, making reasoning replayable, auditable, and mergeable. It also empirically tests whether memory substrates actually improve accuracy across five memory types and benchmarks.

entry.title: Rethinking Global Average Pooling: Your Classifier Is Secretly a Multi-Instance Learner

author.name: Aray Karjauv

entry.summary: This paper shows that standard image classifiers using global average pooling plus a linear head are secretly multi-instance learners, retaining recoverable spatial class evidence even when image-level predictions are wrong. It exploits this to decompose images and learn multi-object tasks from single labels.

entry.title: Trimodal Glioma Representation Alignment via Volumetric Contrastive Learning

author.name: Denise Marini, Eleonora Grassucci, Danilo Comminiello

entry.summary: GLORIA is a trimodal contrastive learning framework aligning histopathology, gene expression, and 3D MRI for glioma grading and survival prediction using a Gramian contrastive loss for joint (not just pairwise) alignment. It integrates heterogeneous biological scales for improved prognosis.

entry.title: When Errors Become Narratives: A Longitudinal Taxonomy of Silent Failures in a Production LLM Agent Runtime

author.name: Wei Wu

entry.summary: This longitudinal study documents silent failures in a real production LLM agent runtime over eight weeks, deriving a five-class mechanism-oriented taxonomy from 22 incidents where error signals never reached humans in actionable form. It provides rare real-world operational insight into agent reliability.

entry.title: Can Editing 1 Neuron Fix Repetition Loops in LLMs?

author.name: Aristotelis Lazaridis, Aman Sharma, Dylan Bates, Brian King, Vincent Lu, Jack FitzGerald

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether repetition loops in Gemma-4 instruction-tuned models during long enumeration tasks can be fixed by editing weights, localizing the failure to a small set of MLP neurons. Editing one neuron helps repetition but does not cure deeper doom loops.

entry.title: A fully GPU-based workflow for building physics emulators of hypersonic flows

author.name: Fabian Paischer, Dylan Rubini, Deniz A. Bezgin, Aaron B. Buhendwa, David Hauser, Florian Sestak, Johannes Brandstetter, Sebastian Kaltenbach, Nikolaus A. Adams

entry.summary: This paper introduces a fully GPU-based workflow integrating accelerated data generation with neural emulator training augmented by uncertainty quantification and physics-aware refinement for hypersonic flows. It targets accurate prediction of shock location and intensity that defeats prior emulators.

entry.title: Scalable Deep Unfolding of Conic Optimizers

author.name: Alex Oshin, Rahul Vodeb Ghosh, Evangelos A. Theodorou

entry.summary: Extends deep unfolding to large-scale semidefinite programs by addressing memory and numerical instability in backpropagating through conic solvers. Uses matrix-free implicit differentiation to make learned SDP solvers scalable for robotics.

entry.title: Overhead Wildlife Locator (OWL): Benchmarking Weakly Supervised Learning for Aerial Wildlife Surveys

author.name: Isai Daniel Chac\'on, Zhongqi Miao, Bruno Demuro, Caleb Robinson, Rahul Dodhia, Lasha Otarashvili, Jason Holmberg, Kirk Larsen, Howard Frederick, Nathan J. Pamperin, Pablo Arbel\'aez, Juan M. Lavista Ferres

entry.summary: OWL is a weakly supervised density-estimation framework for aerial wildlife surveys with three variants (convolutional, Swin-hybrid, and DINOv3-based) using cheaper point-level labels instead of bounding boxes. Benchmarked against detectors across five aerial datasets.

entry.title: Learning Dynamic Swing-Up of an Inverted Pendulum using Remote Magnetic Actuation

author.name: Viacheslav Sydora, Jasan Zughaibi, Denis von Arx, Quentin Boehler, Michael Muehlebach

entry.summary: Demonstrates the first dynamic swing-up of a magnetically actuated inverted pendulum using a clinically-ready electromagnetic navigation system, combining trajectory optimization with learning. The torque/force-based control approach is applicable to catheters and guidewires.

entry.title: High-Fidelity Video Compression based on Invertible Neural Transform and Implicit Conditioning

author.name: Siyue Teng, Ho Man Kwan, Yuxuan Jiang, Fan Zhang, David Bull

entry.summary: InnVC is an invertible-neural-network video codec that preserves an invertible main transform path before quantization while injecting content-adaptive context via implicit conditioning. Targets high-fidelity compression where transform-induced distortion dominates over quantization error.

entry.title: Applicability Condition Extraction for Therapeutic Drug-Disease Relations

author.name: Guanting Luo, Noriki Nishida, Yuji Matsumoto, Yuki Arase

entry.summary: Introduces the task of extracting applicability conditions for therapeutic drug-disease relations from biomedical literature, beyond just identifying the relations themselves. Provides the first annotated dataset of drug-disease-condition triples and evaluates existing methods.

entry.title: GAIT: Legged Robot Proprioceptive State Estimation with Attention over Inertial-Leg Tokens

author.name: Young-Rang Seo, Hajun Kim, Sangmin Kim, Dongyun Kang and Hae-Won Park

entry.summary: Proposes GAIT, an attention-based proprioceptive state estimator for legged robots that tokenizes inertial and leg-wise measurements as individual tokens, letting attention reweight measurements by contact condition. Unlike conventional contact-aided estimators it learns this behavior implicitly rather than via explicit contact detection.

entry.title: A Robust Point Cloud Analysis Framework Inspired By Primary Visual Cortex

author.name: Jisheng Dang and Dengyue Pan and Delin Deng and Yifan Zhang and Bimei Wang and Hong Peng and Bin Hu and Qi Tian and Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: This work introduces a hierarchical Bayesian framework (NLBST) for continuous spatio-temporal forecasting with explicit nonlocal coupling, using a coordinate-based spatial basis and a continuous-time ODE coefficient process. It retains tractable inference for irregular, sparse observations with uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: Communication Policy Evolution for Proactive LLM Agents

author.name: Xinbei Ma, Jiyang Qiu, Yao Yao, Zheng Wu, Yijie Lu, Xiangmou Qu, Jiaxin Yin, Xingyu Lou, Jun Wang, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang, Zhuosheng Zhang, Hai Zhao

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Communication Policy for proactive LLM agents, establishing textual and UI-based policies and evaluating them across environments, personas, and model combinations. It finds text aids task performance while structured UI improves response quality in User-Agent and Planner-Executor settings.

entry.title: More with LESS -- Local Scene Representations for Tactile Imaging

author.name: Zohar Rimon and Elisei Shafer and Tal Tepper and Daniel Kozin and Alon Malka and Roy Holland and Aviv Tamar

entry.summary: LESS is an object-centric tactile imaging representation that models the tactile scene as a grid of recurrent local encoders fused to reconstruct internal structure of soft objects. Its compositional local design enables generalization from single-inclusion training to multi-inclusion objects.

entry.title: ForceForget: Reinforcement Concept Removal for Enhancing Safety in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Dong Han, Yong Li

entry.summary: ForceForget uses reinforcement learning to optimize a concept-erasing reward for safer text-to-image generation while preserving benign concepts via a Safe Adapter projecting partial text embeddings in cross-attention. It targets over-erasure that harms model utility.

entry.title: FLaRA: Predicting Future Latent Representations for Accident Anticipation

author.name: Lorenzo Caselli, Tomaso Trinci, Tommaso Bianconcini, Simone Magistri, Leonardo Taccari, Francesco Sambo, Andrew D. Bagdanov

entry.summary: FLaRA predicts future latent representations for traffic accident anticipation by conditioning a V-JEPA2-based predictor on observed frames and classifying predicted future features. It explicitly models scene evolution rather than directly mapping context to collision probability.

entry.title: Code Correctness Signals in LLM Hidden States: Pre-Generation Probing and Repair Geometry

author.name: Carlo Di Cicco

entry.summary: This work probes whether code correctness is linearly decodable from Qwen3-4B hidden states before generation and during repair, finding a leakage-free held-out AUC around 0.93 even after controlling for prompt length. It uses residualization to isolate genuine correctness signals from confounds.

entry.title: ORCA: A Platform for Open-Source Dexterity Research

author.name: Francesco Capuano, Maximilian Eberlein, Fabrice Bourquin, Clemens Claudio Christoph

entry.summary: ORCA is an open-source research stack for dexterous robotic hand learning, providing integrated software for control, simulation, teleoperation, and retargeting connected to the broader robot-learning ecosystem. It lowers the barrier to using anthropomorphic hands in learning research.

entry.title: The Few-shot Dilemma: Over-prompting Large Language Models

author.name: Yongjian Tang, Doruk Tuncel, Christian Koerner, Thomas Runkler

entry.summary: The paper documents over-prompting, where adding excessive few-shot examples degrades LLM performance, contradicting the assumption that more relevant examples always help. It evaluates random, embedding, and TF-IDF selection across many models including GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, and Llama variants.

entry.title: Efficient On-Device Diffusion LLM Inference with Mobile NPU

author.name: Tuowei Wang, Yanfan Sun, Ju Ren

entry.summary: llada.cpp is presented as the first NPU-aware inference framework for accelerating diffusion LLMs on smartphones, addressing token commitment, KV-cache reuse, and limited NPU address space. It aligns block-wise dLLM inference with mobile NPU execution characteristics.

entry.title: MA-ProofBench: A Two-Tiered Evaluation of LLMs for Theorem Proving in Mathematical Analysis

author.name: Lushi Pu, Weiming Zhang, Xinheng Xie, Zixuan Fu, Bingxiang He, Hongya Lyu, Xin Li, Jie Zhou, and Yudong Wang

entry.summary: MA-ProofBench is presented as the first formal theorem-proving benchmark dedicated to mathematical analysis, with 200 formalized theorems across 6 topics and 27 subcategories at two difficulty levels. It addresses the gap in benchmarks beyond algebra and elementary number theory.

entry.title: Efficient Domain-Adaptive Policy Learning via Kernel Representation with Application to Quadrotor Control under Non-Stationary Disturbances

author.name: Hongyu Zhou, Mingtian Tan, Vasileios Tzoumas

entry.summary: Presents a kernel-based domain-adaptive policy learning method using random Fourier features for quadrotor control under non-stationary disturbances like gusts and payload shifts. Balances expressiveness during offline training with fast online adaptation.

entry.title: How do Self-Supervised Remote Sensing Vision Models Transfer to Downstream Tasks?

author.name: Julia Romero, Qin Lv, Morteza Karimzadeh

entry.summary: Studies how six self-supervised geospatial foundation models transfer to downstream classification, regression, and segmentation tasks, finding model rankings change across tasks and that intermediate transformer layers often carry more task-relevant information. Provides layerwise probing insights.

entry.title: Side-Channel Attacks Bypass Protection in 3D Printers

author.name: Eric Yocam, Varghese Vaidyan, Micah Flack, Gurcan Comert, and Judith L. Mwakalonge

entry.summary: First empirical evaluation of deployed Active Motor Noise Cancellation in commercial 3D printers as an acoustic side-channel countermeasure, finding it fully neutralizes the acoustic channel but the unprotected vibration channel still leaks IP information. Uses a public dataset from AMNC-equipped printers.

entry.title: CaricHarmony: Contrastive Diffusion Paths for Identity-Preserving Caricature Synthesis

author.name: Dongyu Wang, Dar-Yen Chen, Yi-Zhe Song

entry.summary: CaricHarmony is a training-free caricature synthesis method that resolves destructive interference between identity and shape conditions by maintaining three parallel uncontaminated diffusion paths (pure identity, pure shape, harmonized). It uses novel energy functions to prevent collapse.

entry.title: An Attention-based Model for Robust Forecasting with Missing Modality

author.name: Zhitian Zhang, Wenjie Zi, Yunduz Rakhmangulova, Saghar Irandoust, Hossein Hajimirsadeghi, Thibaut Durand

entry.summary: Introduces an attention-based conditional variational autoencoder for robust multimodal forecasting that handles missing modalities during both training and inference. Targets real-world robotic systems with incomplete sensor data.

entry.title: Mask, Sample, Revise: A Revisable CTMC Inference Stack for Guided Discrete Flow Matching Text-to-Speech

author.name: Alef Iury Siqueira Ferreira, Lucas Rafael Stefanel Gris, Luiz Fernando de Ara\'ujo Vidal, Frederico Santos de Oliveira, Christopher Dane Shulby, Anderson da Silva Soares, Arlindo Rodrigues Galv\~ao Filho

entry.summary: Proposes Mask, Sample, Revise, an inference-time control stack for alignment-free discrete flow matching text-to-speech, combining predictor-free guidance, prompt-matched conditional coupling, and a schedule-constrained remasking method. Improves stable low-step conditional speech infilling.

entry.title: ViT-Up: Faithful Feature Upsampling for Vision Transformers

author.name: Krispin Wandel, Jingchuan Wang, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: ViT-Up is an implicit feature upsampling framework for Vision Transformers that replaces external image guidance with layer-wise internal features to avoid feature leakage, fragmentation, and blur in dense prediction tasks. It addresses the bottleneck of small patch-token grids for segmentation and depth estimation.

entry.title: FoleyGenEx: Unified Video-to-Audio Generation with Multi-Modal Control, Temporal Alignment, and Semantic Precision

author.name: Shiyao Wang, Xijuan Zeng, Hui Wang, Shiwan Zhao, Feng Deng, Chen Zhang, Yong Qin

entry.summary: FoleyGenEx is a unified video-to-audio generation framework integrating multimodal control, frame-level temporal alignment, and fine-grained semantics for synchronized audio synthesis. It introduces conditional injection, dynamic masking, and an adverb-based data augmentation algorithm using signal processing and LLMs.

entry.title: FEMOT: Multi-Object Tracking using Frame and Event Cameras

author.name: Shiao Wang, Xiao Wang, Chao Wang, Yitao Li, Menghao Liu, Bo Jiang, Yaowei Wang, Yonghong Tian, Jin Tang

entry.summary: Proposes FEMOT, a large-scale RGB-event multi-object tracking dataset covering diverse scenarios and 14 challenging attributes with high-quality annotations. It addresses the underexploration of RGB-event tracking by combining conventional cameras with high-temporal-resolution event cameras for robustness under motion blur and extreme lighting.

entry.title: BIM-Loc: BIM-Integrated Discrepancy-Aware LiDAR-based Indoor Localization

author.name: Yinqiang Zhang, Liang Lu, Yipeng Pan, Maolin Lei, Yuhan Xie, Zhanteng Xie, Xiaowei Luo, Jia Pan

entry.summary: BIM-Loc is a discrepancy-aware LiDAR localization method that integrates Building Information Models from the design phase, jointly estimating trajectories and online discrepancies between observations and as-designed plans. It targets feature-sparse indoor environments lacking precise maps.

entry.title: Robust Fall Recovery for Armless Bipedal-Wheeled Robots Via Force-Guided Learning

author.name: Haidong Hou, Zhangguo Yu, Tao Han, Hengbo Qi, Khaleel Ghazal, Yu Zhang, Yidong Du, Xuechao Chen, and Fei Meng

entry.summary: FTSR is a force-guided teacher-student framework with stage-wise rewards for fall recovery in armless bipedal-wheeled robots that must rely solely on leg actuation. It uses a simulation auxiliary force correlated with robot height as an optimizable constraint.

entry.title: Achieving Precise Text-To-Cypher Via Grounded Knowledge Graph Data Generation

author.name: Francesco Cazzaro, Jessica Lennon, Ariadna Quattoni

entry.summary: This work presents automatic synthetic data generation grounded in knowledge graphs to fine-tune small LLMs for Text-to-Cypher parsing of property graphs. It shows small locally-deployable models can rival larger proprietary ones on major benchmarks.

entry.title: Recovery thresholds for hidden weighted sparse graphs

author.name: Zhe Hou, Jingcheng Liu

entry.summary: This paper characterizes information-theoretic recovery thresholds for a graph hidden in a randomly weighted complete graph under general edge-weight distributions. It provides a unified characterization assuming local Lipschitzness of Renyi divergence and mild density conditions.

entry.title: IndustryBench-MIPU: Benchmarking Multi-Image Attribute Value Extraction for Industrial Products

author.name: Haonan Qi, Jin Cao, Yongqi Zhang, Xintong Wang, Weidong Tang, Bin Chen, Chengfu Huo, Haojun Pan, Hengyu You, Jing Li, Yingde Wang, Liang Ding

entry.summary: IndustryBench-MIPU is a large-scale benchmark for multi-image industrial product understanding, requiring extraction of property-value pairs from specification tables, nameplates, and technical drawings. It probes MLLM text recognition, visual reasoning, and domain knowledge in industrial contexts.

entry.title: Discovery under Hypothesis Redundancy: A Geometric Theory of Discovery Bottlenecks

author.name: Li Xia and Baoxun Wang

entry.summary: This paper develops a geometric theory of discovery bottlenecks, proposing the Search Compression Hypothesis that non-local LLM-generated exploration helps only when spectral compression, orthogonal escape, and residual signal alignment co-occur. It tests the mechanism on synthetic, financial factor discovery, and symbolic-regression benchmarks.

entry.title: The Perceived Fragility of Explanations in Audio Models: Manipulation of Attribution with Unchanged Predictions

author.name: Piotr Kit{\l}owski, Dominik Wi\k{a}cek, Mateusz Modrzejewski

entry.summary: This paper shows that post-hoc explanations in audio deepfake detectors are fragile: inaudible psychoacoustic perturbations can distort attribution heatmaps while preserving the model prediction. It introduces a domain-specific framework for attacking audio explanations.

entry.title: LoSoNA: A Benchmark for Local Social Norm Adaptation in Group Conversations

author.name: Mateusz Winiarek, Maksymilian Bilski, Mateusz Jacniacki

entry.summary: LoSoNA is a benchmark testing whether LLM-based agents can recognize and adapt to implicit local social norms demonstrated in multi-party group chats, evaluating eight models under four prompting conditions. It finds naive prompting limited for most models, exposing gaps in social norm inference.

entry.title: Orchestra-o1: Omnimodal Agent Orchestration

author.name: Fan Zhang, Vireo Zhang, Shengju Qian, Haoxuan Li, Hao Wu, Jinyang Wu, Donghao Zhou, Zhihong Zhu, Zheng Lian, Xin Wang, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: Orchestra-o1 is an omnimodal agent orchestration framework that coordinates specialized agents across text, image, audio, and video for complex tasks where heterogeneous modalities interact. It extends multi-agent orchestration beyond narrow modality sets.

entry.title: Connections Between Pairs of Filters Improve the Accuracy of Convolutional Neural Networks

author.name: Kathleen Anderson, Philipp Gr\"uning, Erhardt Barth

entry.summary: FreoStream is a streaming guardrail framework that uses a LoRA-based Future-Aware Reasoning module to predict future content before judging token-level safety, reducing over-refusal while catching implicitly harmful jailbreak content. It follows a predict-reason-judge paradigm.

entry.title: The Program Is Still There: A Conservation Law for Program Discovery

author.name: Jorge Miguel Silva

entry.summary: This paper defines a coupling-width measure for program-discovery search and proves an unconditional exponential worst-case lower bound, yielding a conservation law where injected structural knowledge trades one-for-one against required search. It reframes program-search uncomputability as a measurable price.

entry.title: Uncertainty Estimation and Generalization Bounds for Modern Deep Learning

author.name: Luis A. Ortega

entry.summary: A doctoral thesis unifying Bayesian inference, function-space modeling, and large-deviation theory to study uncertainty quantification and generalization in deep learning. It introduces methods like Deep Variational Implicit Processes and post-hoc Laplace/GP approximations.

entry.title: Crypto x AI, AI x Crypto: A Survey

author.name: Sarah Allen, Pranay Anchuri, James Austgen, Maryam Bahrani, Samuel Breckenridge, Aaron Buchwald, Christian Cachin, Andr\'es F\'abrega, Jared Fernandez, James Hsin-yu Chiang, Marwa Mouallem, Roi Bar-Zur, Neil DeSilva, Ittay Eyal, Giulia Fanti, Ari Juels, Andrew Miller, Christian Sillaber, Dani Vilardell, Pramod Viswanath, Wenhao Wang, Matt Weinberg, Sen Yang, Jianzhu Yao, and Fan Zhang

entry.summary: A broad survey systematizing the intersection of crypto/blockchain and AI in both directions, summarizing accomplishments, opportunities, challenges, and industry misconceptions. Concludes the integration remains in very early stages.

entry.title: PMOF: A Dataset and Benchmark for Passenger Monitoring Using Overhead Fisheye Cameras

author.name: Stella Katharina Wermuth, Qazi Arbab Ahmed, Klaus Neumann, Thorsten Jungeblut

entry.summary: PMOF is the first public dataset of top-view fisheye imagery captured inside a moving vehicle for passenger monitoring, with over 19k annotated frames including rotated bounding boxes and tracking. It captures motion-induced domain shift absent from static fisheye datasets.

entry.title: The Holistic Storage of Verb+Up Phrases in Text-based and Audio-based Language Models

author.name: Zachary Nicholas Houghton, Yu Zhou, Dan Pluth, Vijay K. Gurbani

entry.summary: Probes internal representations in text-based LLMs and an ASR model to test whether verb+up phrasal verbs develop holistic stored representations as a function of frequency and predictability. Finds evidence of holistic storage supporting usage-based theories of language.

entry.title: Anytime-Valid Confirmation of Label-Shift Corrections

author.name: Seungjin Choi

entry.summary: Develops an anytime-valid sequential test to confirm whether incoming labeled outcomes support a pre-specified label-shift correction, using a conditional e-value and martingale via Ville's inequality. It converts routine model monitoring into a formal statistical test for small-batch scientific deployments.

entry.title: Deep Spectral Learning of Embedded Latent Transfer Operators for Stochastic Dynamical Systems

author.name: Ryogo Tanaka, Yoshinobu Kawahara

entry.summary: Proposes Deep Spectral Encoder, an operator-based latent state-space model for stochastic nonlinear dynamical systems using learnable neural feature maps and transfer/observation operators. Uses functional canonical correlation analysis in a Galerkin-projected feature space with closed-form ridge-regularized operator estimation.

entry.title: Context-aware Modality-Topology Co-Alignment for Multimodal Attributed Graphs

author.name: Sirui Zhang, Xu Wang, Zhengyu Wu, Xunkai Li, Hongchao Qin

entry.summary: Proposes CoMAG, a unified backbone for multimodal attributed graphs that learns task-adaptive reliable contexts and modality-preserving alignment, addressing fixed graph contexts and over-compressed fusion in prior methods. It estimates edge reliability for reliable context learning to serve both graph-centric and modality-centric tasks.

entry.title: MeEvo: Metacognitive Evolution Combined with Natural Evolution for Automatic Heuristic Design

author.name: Zishang Qiu, Xinan Chen, Rong Qu, Ruibin Bai

entry.summary: MeEvo combines metacognitive (reflection-based) and natural (crossover/mutation) evolution in a dual-layer framework for LLM-based automatic heuristic design. It preserves reasoning traces while enabling population-level recombination to improve search efficiency.

entry.title: SyLink Hand: A Synergy-Inspired Linkage-Driven Anthropomorphic Hand for Human-Like Dexterity

author.name: Hao Wu, Yanzhe Wang, Yu Feng, Yitong Li, Jingxiang Guo, Jian Liu, and Jianshu Zhou

entry.summary: SyLink Hand is an anthropomorphic dexterous hand integrating biomechanical synergy principles with linkage-driven transmission to achieve human-like dexterity in a compact, low-cost design. Motion-capture analysis of hand synergies guides a simplified DOF configuration.

entry.title: Does the Judge Prefer English? Evaluating Language-Switching Invariance in LLM-as-a-Judge

author.name: Shaojie Yin
